71:21.ar: قَالَ نُوحࣱ رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمۡ عَصَوۡنِي وَٱتَّبَعُواْ مَن لَّمۡ يَزِدۡهُ مَالُهُۥ وَوَلَدُهُۥٓ إِلَّا خَسَارࣰ ا
71:21.en: Noah said: My Lord! Lo! they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children increase him in naught save ruin

71:22.en: And they have plotted a mighty plot

71:23.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمۡ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدࣰّ ا وَلَا سُوَاعࣰ ا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسۡرࣰ ا
71:23.en: And they have said: Forsake not your gods. Forsake not Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr

71:24.ar: وَقَدۡ أَضَلُّواْ كَثِيرࣰ اۖ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَٰلࣰ ا
71:24.en: And they have led many astray, and Thou increasest the wrong-doers in naught save error

71:25.ar: مِّمَّا خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمۡ أُغۡرِقُواْ فَأُدۡخِلُواْ نَارࣰ ا فَلَمۡ يَجِدُواْ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَنصَارࣰ ا
71:25.en: Because of their sins they were drowned, then made to enter a Fire. And they found they had no helpers in place of Allah

71:26.ar: وَقَالَ نُوحࣱ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرۡ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا
71:26.en: And Noah said: My Lord! Leave not one of the disbelievers in the land

71:27.ar: إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرۡهُمۡ يُضِلُّواْ عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوٓاْ إِلَّا فَاجِرࣰ ا كَفَّارࣰ ا
71:27.en: If Thou shouldst leave them, they will mislead Thy slaves and will beget none save lewd ingrates

71:28.ar: رَّبِّ ٱغۡفِرۡ لِي وَلِوَٰلِدَيَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيۡتِيَ مُؤۡمِنࣰ ا وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِۖ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارَۢا
71:28.en: My Lord! Forgive me and my parents and him who entereth my house believing, and believing men and believing women, and increase not the wrong-doers in aught save ruin

71:10.ar: فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارࣰ ا
71:10.en: And I have said: Seek pardon of your Lord. Lo! He was ever Forgiving

71:11.en: He will let loose the sky for you in plenteous rain

71:12.ar: وَيُمۡدِدۡكُم بِأَمۡوَٰلࣲ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ أَنۡهَٰرࣰ ا
71:12.en: And will help you with wealth and sons, and will assign unto you Gardens and will assign unto you rivers

71:13.ar: مَّا لَكُمۡ لَا تَرۡجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارࣰ ا
71:13.en: What aileth you that ye hope not toward Allah for dignity

71:14.en: When He created you by (divers) stages

71:15.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَوۡاْ كَيۡفَ خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ طِبَاقࣰ ا
71:15.en: See ye not how Allah hath created seven heavens in harmony

71:16.ar: وَجَعَلَ ٱلۡقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورࣰ ا وَجَعَلَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ سِرَاجࣰ ا
71:16.en: And hath made the moon a light therein, and made the sun a lamp

71:17.ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ نَبَاتࣰ ا
71:17.en: And Allah hath caused you to grow as a growth from the earth

71:18.ar: ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمۡ فِيهَا وَيُخۡرِجُكُمۡ إِخۡرَاجࣰ ا
71:18.en: And afterward He maketh you return thereto, and He will bring you forth again, a (new) forthbringing

71:19.ar: وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِسَاطࣰ ا
71:19.en: And Allah hath made the earth a wide expanse for you

71:20.ar: لِّتَسۡلُكُواْ مِنۡهَا سُبُلࣰ ا فِجَاجࣰ ا
71:20.en: That ye may thread the valley-ways thereof

29:20.ar: قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ بَدَأَ ٱلۡخَلۡقَۚ ثُمَّ ٱللَّهُ يُنشِئُ ٱلنَّشۡأَةَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
29:20.en: Say (O Muhammad): Travel in the land and see how He originated creation, then Allah bringeth forth the later growth. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things

2:165.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا يُحِبُّونَهُمۡ كَحُبِّ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَشَدُّ حُبࣰّ ا لِّلَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِذۡ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَنَّ ٱلۡقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
2:165.en: Yet of mankind are some who take unto themselves (objects of worship which they set as) rivals to Allah, loving them with a love like (that which is the due) of Allah (only) - those who believe are stauncher in their love for Allah - Oh, that those who do evil had but known, (on the day) when they behold the doom, that power belongeth wholly to Allah, and that Allah is severe in punishment

11:27.ar: فَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرࣰ ا مِّثۡلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِيَ ٱلرَّأۡيِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمۡ عَلَيۡنَا مِن فَضۡلِۭ بَلۡ نَظُنُّكُمۡ كَٰذِبِينَ
11:27.en: The chieftains of his folk, who disbelieved, said: We see thee but a mortal like us, and we see not that any follow thee save the most abject among us, without reflection. We behold in you no merit above us - nay, we deem you liars

10:88.ar: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ ءَاتَيۡتَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَمَلَأَهُۥ زِينَةࣰ وَأَمۡوَٰلࣰ ا فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِكَۖ رَبَّنَا ٱطۡمِسۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ وَٱشۡدُدۡ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمۡ فَلَا يُؤۡمِنُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ ٱلۡأَلِيمَ
10:88.en: And Moses said: Our Lord! Lo! Thou hast given Pharaoh and his chiefs splendour and riches in the life of the world, Our Lord! that they may lead men astray from Thy way. Our Lord! Destroy their riches and harden their hearts so that they believe not till they see the painful doom

11:36.ar: وَأُوحِيَ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ أَنَّهُۥ لَن يُؤۡمِنَ مِن قَوۡمِكَ إِلَّا مَن قَدۡ ءَامَنَ فَلَا تَبۡتَئِسۡ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
11:36.en: And it was inspired in Noah, (saying): No-one of thy folk will believe save him who hath believed already. Be not distressed because of what they do

11:37.ar: وَٱصۡنَعِ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَا وَوَحۡيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبۡنِي فِي ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِنَّهُم مُّغۡرَقُونَ
11:37.en: Build the ship under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, and speak not unto Me on behalf of those who do wrong. Lo! they will be drowned

ZGjVxjCfZ40.title: Surat Nuh Part 3: Verses 21-28
ZGjVxjCfZ40.one_line: Why Nuh's people refused: following wealth and power, a vast plot of distraction, and five idols read as passion, time, desire, fear and admiration.
ZGjVxjCfZ40.summary: Concluding Surat Nuh, he presents the final verses as Nuh's report of the outcome after proving the quantity, quality and content of his work. His people disobeyed him and followed someone else, unnamed because the description matters more than the name: a man whose wealth and children only increased his loss. Humans, he argues, always follow someone, true freedom is following the One who frees you from everyone else, and people are dazzled by financial and social power, which is why most prophets had neither. Khasar is losing where one expected to win, the fate of those who chase power for its own sake. The great plot of Nuh's opponents is still with us: hunger and fear in some lands, endless entertainment, gaming and social media in others, keeping people content and unquestioning; Nuh lost his own son to it. He reads the five names Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr through their meanings as the five things that distract people: passion, careless use of time, desire, fear and admiration. Nuh never compromised his principles to win followers, and Muslims must not remove Islam's edge to make it attractive. He explains Nuh's final dua, cautions that only prophets may pray for oppressors' misguidance, and ends with the believers as Nuh's true household.

outline.heading: Memorising the last part of the Quran
outline.gist: The series has worked through these surahs slowly so people can understand and memorise them; the cluster's first four surahs set the requirements, and two examples of dawah follow.

outline.heading: Beginning of time and end of time
outline.gist: Nuh at the start of history and the Prophet at its end faced the same struggles, showing human nature has barely changed despite technology.

outline.heading: Recap: istighfar as a practical system
outline.gist: Nuh began with a command that benefits people religiously or pragmatically: daily self-correction that improves individuals and communities.

outline.heading: Recap: respect for Allah through studying creation
outline.gist: Lack of respect for the one who drew the lines prevents real repentance; Nuh directed people to the open book of creation.

outline.heading: Physicians who do not believe
outline.gist: The intricacy of the human body, which no one controls, should produce awe and accountability before a Creator beyond any titan.

outline.heading: From effort to outcome
outline.gist: Having shown the quantity, quality and content of his work, Nuh now reports the result. A tajweed note on the verse.

outline.heading: They disobeyed me and followed another
outline.gist: Nuh is still speaking to Allah, explaining why so few followed.

outline.heading: Everyone follows someone: true freedom
outline.gist: Free spirits follow ways laid down before them; real freedom is following the One who can liberate you from everything else.

outline.heading: Why the Quran leaves him unnamed
outline.gist: When a name is withheld the description is the lesson; chasing names makes us miss it.

outline.heading: Prophets first called people to study the world
outline.gist: Nuh, then Ibrahim, were the first on record to urge people to observe and learn, so what could draw people away from that?

outline.heading: What could outweigh Nuh's call
outline.gist: His message was simple and good for anyone with a clean fitrah, so the rival must have offered something compelling.

outline.heading: Wealth and children: financial and social strength
outline.gist: The Quran's two domains of strength; losing one makes you a miskin or an orphan in need of care.

outline.heading: Caring for orphans
outline.gist: Some orphans lack both wealth and family, and the Prophet promised closeness in Paradise to whoever sponsors them.

outline.heading: People switch off their minds for power
outline.gist: Someone with both wealth and many children sways people regardless of what he says, as an unqualified but powerful president shows.

outline.heading: Why prophets lacked wealth and sons
outline.gist: Abu Jahl had more sons than he could count while the Prophet's sons died young; people were to be drawn to principles, not power.

outline.heading: Khasar: losing where you expected to win
outline.gist: His power only increased his loss, a loss specifically where he thought his tools would bring victory.

outline.heading: The blinding pursuit of power
outline.gist: Seeking power as an end rather than a means is the downfall of great men and a bad transaction.

outline.heading: A humongous plot
outline.gist: Kubbar is the strongest intensive form: a plot that answered every question so people stayed misdirected and impressed by the wrong things.

outline.heading: Kept content while the world burns
outline.gist: Today people stay distracted and blissfully ignorant while the rich grow richer, the planet heats and oppression continues.

outline.heading: Hunger and fear or entertainment
outline.gist: Where he grew up people were kept busy chasing bread under fear; here a trillion-dollar entertainment, sports, gaming and travel industry does the job.

outline.heading: Social media flexing and Nuh's lost son
outline.gist: Social media displays empty power and breeds discontent; Nuh grieves that the plot took his own son and wife.

outline.heading: Every generation equally distracted
outline.gist: The tools change from arena to radio to phone, but the distraction is the same.

outline.heading: Do not abandon your gods: the five names
outline.gist: Scholars said the five were righteous people later worshipped, or idols of major Arab tribes, among other views.

outline.heading: Why the five names are listed separately
outline.gist: Listing them after the general word for gods suggests more than idols; their meanings together map what humans get obsessed by.

outline.heading: Wadd: passion and romantic love
outline.gist: Emotional and sexual passion blinds people to right and wrong more than anything.

outline.heading: Love that overrides what is right
outline.gist: Doing haram to provide for family is not heroic; feeding them haram is not love. Allah and the Prophet must be loved first.

outline.heading: Suwa': the problem of time
outline.gist: Thinking we have plenty of time leads to a shallow life; fearing age leads to grabbing all we can now.

outline.heading: Why the young are absent from the masjid
outline.gist: Elders fill masajid while youth feel time is on their side; procrastination is the disease of time.

outline.heading: Yaghuth: what you desire
outline.gist: Ghawth is help you plead for intensely: the things you want badly.

outline.heading: Ya'uq: what you fear
outline.gist: From preventing something: the barrier you want against what you dread.

outline.heading: Nasr: what you admire
outline.gist: The eagle symbolises admired strength and is the commonest animal on national flags, even where eagles are long gone.

outline.heading: Five categories that capture every distraction
outline.gist: Passion, time, desire, fear and admiration cover how people lose focus; the opponents kept people chasing them.

outline.heading: We cannot get our children to listen
outline.gist: The same machine operates in London and the Middle East, perhaps worse there.

outline.heading: Islam demands questioning the status quo
outline.gist: Allah's teachings require questioning what is unhealthy and standing against corruption of every kind.

outline.heading: Nuh refused to drop his poor followers
outline.gist: Elites offered to listen if he expelled the poor; he never traded a principle for converts.

outline.heading: Never sell Islam without its edge
outline.gist: Presenting Islam as tolerant of oppression or shirk to make it attractive misrepresents it; if people refuse, they refuse.

outline.heading: A quarter of Nuh's effort would transform us
outline.gist: Nuh did everything right and still failed because outcomes were never in his hand; they misguided many.

outline.heading: A dua reserved for prophets
outline.gist: Asking Allah to increase oppressors in misguidance came from a bleeding heart; most scholars restrict it to prophets like Nuh and Musa, while others may pray for oppression to end.

outline.heading: Drowned for their conscious sins
outline.gist: Khati'at are sins done knowingly; it was their sins that drowned them and sent them to the Fire with no helper besides Allah.

outline.heading: Leave none of them on the earth
outline.gist: Dayyar are those settled in their ways; the problem was not disbelief alone but that they would misguide others and raise children without ethics or faith.

outline.heading: The prophet who forgave his people
outline.gist: The Prophet told of a prophet, beaten bloody, who prayed for his people's forgiveness because they did not know.

outline.heading: Why Nuh finally prayed against them
outline.gist: Nuh is the only prophet told to stop speaking to Allah about the oppressors; only when Allah removed all hope did he ask that they be taken away.

outline.heading: Forgive me, my parents and my household of faith
outline.gist: Bayt means family; Nuh's household is everyone who enters faith with him, which excludes his son and includes all believers to the end of time.

outline.heading: Mu'adh and the people closest to the Prophet
outline.gist: Sending Mu'adh to Yemen, the Prophet told him the God-fearing are his people wherever they are, echoing Nuh's prayer for all believers.

outline.heading: Outro

17:105.ar: وَبِٱلۡحَقِّ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ وَبِٱلۡحَقِّ نَزَلَۗ وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرࣰ ا وَنَذِيرࣰ ا
17:105.en: With truth have We sent it down, and with truth hath it descended. And We have sent thee as naught else save a bearer of good tidings and a warner

17:106.ar: وَقُرۡءَانࣰ ا فَرَقۡنَٰهُ لِتَقۡرَأَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكۡثࣲ وَنَزَّلۡنَٰهُ تَنزِيلࣰ ا
17:106.en: And (it is) a Qur'an that We have divided, that thou mayst recite it unto mankind at intervals, and We have revealed it by (successive) revelation

17:107.ar: قُلۡ ءَامِنُواْ بِهِۦٓ أَوۡ لَا تُؤۡمِنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦٓ إِذَا يُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡ يَخِرُّونَۤ لِلۡأَذۡقَانِۤ سُجَّدࣰ اۤ
17:107.en: Say: Believe therein or believe not, lo! those who were given knowledge before it, when it is read unto them, fall down prostrate on their faces, adoring

17:108.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ سُبۡحَٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِن كَانَ وَعۡدُ رَبِّنَا لَمَفۡعُولࣰ ا
17:108.en: Saying: Glory to our Lord! Verily the promise of our Lord must be fulfilled

17:109.ar: وَيَخِرُّونَ لِلۡأَذۡقَانِ يَبۡكُونَ وَيَزِيدُهُمۡ خُشُوعࣰ ا۩
17:109.en: They fall down on their faces, weeping, and it increaseth humility in them

17:110.ar: قُلِ ٱدۡعُواْ ٱللَّهَ أَوِ ٱدۡعُواْ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنَۖ أَيࣰّ ا مَّا تَدۡعُواْ فَلَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ وَلَا تَجۡهَرۡ بِصَلَاتِكَ وَلَا تُخَافِتۡ بِهَا وَٱبۡتَغِ بَيۡنَ ذَٰلِكَ سَبِيلࣰ ا
17:110.en: Say (unto mankind): Cry unto Allah, or cry unto the Beneficent, unto whichsoever ye cry (it is the same). His are the most beautiful names. And thou (Muhammad), be not loud-voiced in thy worship nor yet silent therein, but follow a way between

17:111.ar: وَقُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَمۡ يَتَّخِذۡ وَلَدࣰ ا وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكࣱ فِي ٱلۡمُلۡكِ وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلِيࣱّ مِّنَ ٱلذُّلِّۖ وَكَبِّرۡهُ تَكۡبِيرَۢا
17:111.en: And say: Praise be to Allah, Who hath not taken unto Himself a son, and Who hath no partner in the Sovereignty, nor hath He any protecting friend through dependence. And magnify Him with all magnificence

2:286.ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَعَلَيۡهَا مَا ٱكۡتَسَبَتۡۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذۡنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوۡ أَخۡطَأۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡنَآ إِصۡرࣰ ا كَمَا حَمَلۡتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلۡنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦۖ وَٱعۡفُ عَنَّا وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَآۚ أَنتَ مَوۡلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:286.en: Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope. For it (is only) that which it hath earned, and against it (only) that which it hath deserved. Our Lord! Condemn us not if we forget, or miss the mark! Our Lord! Lay not on us such a burden as thou didst lay on those before us! Our Lord! Impose not on us that which we have not the strength to bear! Pardon us, absolve us and have mercy on us, Thou, our Protector, and give us victory over the disbelieving folk

29:45.ar: ٱتۡلُ مَآ أُوحِيَ إِلَيۡكَ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۖ إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنۡهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَٱلۡمُنكَرِۗ وَلَذِكۡرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكۡبَرُۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَصۡنَعُونَ
29:45.en: Recite that which hath been inspired in thee of the Scripture, and establish worship. Lo! worship preserveth from lewdness and iniquity, but verily remembrance of Allah is more important. And Allah knoweth what ye do

20:14.ar: إِنَّنِيٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعۡبُدۡنِي وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكۡرِيٓ
20:14.en: Lo! I, even I, am Allah, There is no Allah save Me. So serve Me and establish worship for My remembrance

32:15.ar: إِنَّمَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِهَا خَرُّواْۤ سُجَّدࣰ اۤ وَسَبَّحُواْ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ۩
32:15.en: Only those believe in Our revelations who, when they are reminded of them, fall down prostrate and hymn the praise of their Lord, and they are not scornful

32:16.ar: تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّهُمۡ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعࣰ ا وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
32:16.en: Who forsake their beds to cry unto their Lord in fear and hope, and spend of that We have bestowed on them

32:17.ar: فَلَا تَعۡلَمُ نَفۡسࣱ مَّآ أُخۡفِيَ لَهُم مِّن قُرَّةِ أَعۡيُنࣲ جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
32:17.en: No soul knoweth what is kept hid for them of joy, as a reward for what they used to do

73:1.en: O thou wrapped up in thy raiment

73:2.en: Keep vigil the night long, save a little

73:3.en: A half thereof, or abate a little thereof

73:4.ar: أَوۡ زِدۡ عَلَيۡهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ تَرۡتِيلًا
73:4.en: Or add (a little) thereto - and chant the Qur'an in measure

73:5.ar: إِنَّا سَنُلۡقِي عَلَيۡكَ قَوۡلࣰ ا ثَقِيلًا
73:5.en: For we shall charge thee with a word of weight

13:28.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَتَطۡمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُم بِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِۗ أَلَا بِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطۡمَئِنُّ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ
13:28.en: Who have believed and whose hearts have rest in the remembrance of Allah. Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest

13:29.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ طُوبَىٰ لَهُمۡ وَحُسۡنُ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
13:29.en: Those who believe and do right: Joy is for them, and bliss (their) journey's end

mQ912XJqDhg.speaker: adnan
mQ912XJqDhg.speaker_note: First-person opening of his 'Achieving the Outcomes' series ('the series I'm going to be sharing with you over the next number of weeks'; 'I talked about attitude last week'); same bilingual khutbah format as the rest of the series; title names no other speaker.
mQ912XJqDhg.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Rituals to Connection
mQ912XJqDhg.one_line: Rituals exist to build a living connection with Allah; prayer that has become mechanical restrains nothing and gives nothing.
mQ912XJqDhg.summary: Episode of 'Achieving the Outcomes', mixed English and Arabic, on taking rituals from mechanics to connection. After reciting Al-Isra 17:105-111 and prostrating, he frames the question: we are accountable for outcomes, and the Quran's stated outcome for hearing revelation is to fall prostrate in tears and grow closer to Allah. If salah, dhikr, fasting and hajj do not produce that, what was their purpose and will they be accepted? He offers questions rather than answers. Al-Ankabut 29:45 says prayer restrains from indecency; Ibn Mas'ud said prayer that does not only adds distance, and the Prophet said of the man who prays at night and steals by day that real prayer would stop him. The relationship with Allah has no parallel: He speaks through the Book, you speak through prayer, He answers through your life. Rituals are not an added burden but the means to carry the covenant, which is why Al-Muzzammil answered the Prophet's terror on the night of the first revelation with the command to stand at night. The Arabic second khutbah mocks the fifteen-second Fatihah and the man who cannot remember whether he prayed Asr, and recalls that prayer was the Prophet's delight and his refuge when troubled. Hearts find rest only in remembrance (13:28). He closes by tying this inner work to the ummah's unity and the removal of oppression: Islam cannot be cherry-picked.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Isra 17:105-111: falling on their chins in tears
outline.gist: He recites the closing verses of Al-Isra and renders them: the Quran sent down in truth and gradually so people reflect; those given knowledge fall on their chins in prostration, weeping, increasing in humility; call Him Allah or Ar-Rahman. Then the prostration of recitation.

outline.heading: Accountable for outcomes within our capacity
outline.gist: Allah burdens no soul beyond its capacity, but effort counts as complete only when aimed at the right outcome; trying your best is not enough if you do not know what you are trying to achieve. Last week was knowledge into attitude.

outline.heading: Rituals and their stated outcome
outline.gist: Salah, recitation, tasbih, dhikr, fasting, zakat and hajj have an outcome the Quran names: hearts that fall prostrate in tears and grow closer to Him. If that is absent, what was their purpose, were they done right, will they be accepted? He offers questions, not answers.

outline.heading: Prayer restrains from indecency
outline.gist: Prayer restrains from indecency and wrong, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. Ibn Mas'ud: whoever's prayer does not restrain him gains nothing from it but distance from Allah.

outline.heading: The man who prays at night and steals by day
outline.gist: Stealing includes cheating people in business and taking more than you deserve. The Prophet said that if the man truly prays, his prayer will stop him; true prayer builds a connection with a God we cannot see.

outline.heading: A relationship without parallel
outline.gist: Every other relationship is with visible creation that responds on time. With Allah, He speaks to you through the Book, you speak to Him through prayer, and He answers through your life, with the evidence shown on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Prayer for My remembrance
outline.gist: If rituals build no connection, what do you gain? Allah told Musa to establish prayer for His remembrance, and describes the believers who fall prostrate when reminded and whose sides forsake their beds.

outline.heading: Sides that forsake their beds
outline.gist: The connected cannot wait to rise at night and speak to Him, calling in fear and hope, knowing only He holds what they seek. Rituals are designed to build exactly that connection.

outline.heading: Connected, sin becomes nearly impossible
outline.gist: When His remembrance and commands are alive inside you, sin and harm become very hard because He is present with you; disconnected, you can do anything. Yet we have reduced rituals to mechanical movements and teach them that way.

outline.heading: Rituals are not an extra burden
outline.gist: We train ourselves to zone out while tongue and muscles perform memorised movements. Rituals are not an added load but the means through which you fulfil your commands and covenant.

outline.heading: Al-Muzzammil: back to the night on the mountain
outline.gist: One of the earliest revelations calls the Prophet by what he did the night he ran down the mountain, cold and afraid, asking his wife to cover him: stand the night, recite slowly, for We will cast upon you a heavy word.

outline.heading: Stand and speak to Me
outline.gist: Stand and talk to Me, complain to Me, tell Me your fears and hopes, and teach your followers the same: the more you do it, the more of the burden you can carry and the lighter it becomes.

outline.heading: From habit to connection
outline.gist: Until a ritual moves from habitual action to connection, it stays a chore. Once it grants something profound in the heart, you no longer need reminding or forcing.

outline.heading: Husks without a soul: what benefit?
outline.gist: If rituals do not become a real link to the Lord, if prayer does not restrain from indecency, bring you closer to Allah, distance you from Shaytan and make good deeds beloved, what benefit has the son of Adam taken from them?

outline.heading: The delight of his eye
outline.gist: The Prophet never saw rituals as a load but as the most beautiful part of his life: the delight of his eye was placed in prayer, he told Bilal to give them rest through it, and when troubled he rushed to prayer as a refuge.

outline.heading: The fifteen-second Fatihah
outline.gist: He found in prayer a link with his Lord found nowhere else. When rituals become soulless habits and husks, the tongue races through Al-Fatihah in fifteen seconds and rotates between the same three short surahs.

outline.heading: You meet Allah and do not remember?
outline.gist: The muscles pray four rak'ahs on their own, and a man cannot say whether he prayed Asr. You remember meeting a person; how do you forget meeting Allah? Many will have their prayers thrown back in their faces.

outline.heading: The King of kings offers you conversation
outline.gist: Allah needs nothing from our prayer; He commanded it so we can be near Him. You cannot reach Him with the senses in this world, only with the heart, the soul that came from Him.

outline.heading: Hearts find rest in His remembrance
outline.gist: A soul occupied with His remembrance finds tranquility, peace and wellbeing here, joined to peace in the Hereafter: in the remembrance of Allah hearts find rest, and good is the end of those who believe and do good.

outline.heading: Everyone carries an instability
outline.gist: Every person has an inner instability and urges toward what does not help them. Remembrance calms it and gives room for good choices; the Prophet asked Bilal for the call so they could find ease, not to get prayer out of the way.

outline.heading: A chest like a boiling pot
outline.gist: When the Prophet prayed, a sound like a boiling pot came from his chest. People with that connection and love carry their burdens and look forward to prayer instead of running from it.

outline.heading: Choose connection, or keep racing
outline.gist: This is what prayer can be if you choose it. Otherwise keep running the hundred-metre dash; you could probably beat Usain Bolt's record and get through your whole life that way.

outline.heading: Spiritual work serves the ummah's outcome
outline.gist: The ummah's goal is to come together, regain strength and unity, remove oppression and right wrongs. A spiritual topic is not a detour from that: these inner changes are what will turn things around, and Islam cannot be cherry-picked.

outline.heading: Outro

quran.point: Opening recitation: the Quran revealed in truth and gradually; those given knowledge fall prostrate weeping and increase in khushu; the stated outcome of hearing revelation that he measures our rituals against.
Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity: we are accountable for outcomes within what we could do.
Establish prayer, for prayer restrains from indecency and wrong, and the remembrance of Allah is greater; prayer that restrains nothing has missed its outcome.
Establish prayer for My remembrance: the purpose of salah is to be in a state of remembering Allah.
Only those truly believe who fall prostrate when reminded, whose sides forsake their beds, who call on their Lord in fear and hope; a picture of the connection rituals are meant to build.
O you wrapped up, stand at night and recite slowly, for We will cast upon you a heavy word: night prayer and recitation are what make the burden carriable.
Hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah; blessed are those who believe and do good. Connection brings tranquility in this world and the next.

Umm Salamah and Aisha: when a matter troubled the Prophet he rushed to prayer as his refuge.

takeaways: Measure your rituals by their outcome: does your prayer restrain you from indecency and wrong and bring you closer to Allah?
Stop treating salah as memorized mechanics; slow down, know what you recite and remember whom you are meeting.
Use prayer as the Prophet did, a refuge to run to when troubled and a rest, not a task to get out of the way.

72:1.ar: قُلۡ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسۡتَمَعَ نَفَرࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا سَمِعۡنَا قُرۡءَانًا عَجَبࣰ ا
72:1.en: Say (O Muhammad): It is revealed unto me that a company of the Jinn gave ear, and they said: Lo! we have heard a marvellous Qur'an

72:2.ar: يَهۡدِيٓ إِلَى ٱلرُّشۡدِ فَـَٔامَنَّا بِهِۦۖ وَلَن نُّشۡرِكَ بِرَبِّنَآ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:2.en: Which guideth unto righteousness, so we believe in it and we ascribe no partner unto our Lord

72:3.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ تَعَٰلَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا مَا ٱتَّخَذَ صَٰحِبَةࣰ وَلَا وَلَدࣰ ا
72:3.en: And (we believe) that He - exalted be the glory of our Lord! - hath taken neither wife nor son

72:4.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ كَانَ يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنَا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ شَطَطࣰ ا
72:4.en: And that the foolish one among us used to speak concerning Allah an atrocious lie

72:5.ar: وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن تَقُولَ ٱلۡإِنسُ وَٱلۡجِنُّ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبࣰ ا
72:5.en: And lo! we had supposed that humankind and jinn would not speak a lie concerning Allah

72:6.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ كَانَ رِجَالࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡإِنسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجَالࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ فَزَادُوهُمۡ رَهَقࣰ ا
72:6.en: And indeed (O Muhammad) individuals of humankind used to invoke the protection of individuals of the jinn, so that they increased them in revolt against Allah

72:7.ar: وَأَنَّهُمۡ ظَنُّواْ كَمَا ظَنَنتُمۡ أَن لَّن يَبۡعَثَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:7.en: And indeed they supposed, even as ye suppose, that Allah would not raise anyone (from the dead)

72:8.ar: وَأَنَّا لَمَسۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ فَوَجَدۡنَٰهَا مُلِئَتۡ حَرَسࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ ا وَشُهُبࣰ ا
72:8.en: And (the Jinn who had listened to the Qur'an said): We had sought the heaven but had found it filled with strong warders and meteors

72:9.ar: وَأَنَّا كُنَّا نَقۡعُدُ مِنۡهَا مَقَٰعِدَ لِلسَّمۡعِۖ فَمَن يَسۡتَمِعِ ٱلۡأٓنَ يَجِدۡ لَهُۥ شِهَابࣰ ا رَّصَدࣰ ا
72:9.en: And we used to sit on places (high) therein to listen. But he who listeneth now findeth a flame in wait for him

72:10.ar: وَأَنَّا لَا نَدۡرِيٓ أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَمۡ أَرَادَ بِهِمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ رَشَدࣰ ا
72:10.en: And we know not whether harm is boded unto all who are in the earth, or whether their Lord intendeth guidance for them

55:15.ar: وَخَلَقَ ٱلۡجَآنَّ مِن مَّارِجࣲ مِّن نَّارࣲ‏
55:15.en: And the jinn did He create of smokeless fire

55:31.en: We shall dispose of you, O ye two dependents (man and jinn)

35:6.ar: إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لَكُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ فَٱتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّاۚ إِنَّمَا يَدۡعُواْ حِزۡبَهُۥ لِيَكُونُواْ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
35:6.en: Lo! the devil is an enemy for you, so treat him as an enemy. He only summoneth his faction to be owners of the flaming Fire

7:27.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ لَا يَفۡتِنَنَّكُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ كَمَآ أَخۡرَجَ أَبَوَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ يَنزِعُ عَنۡهُمَا لِبَاسَهُمَا لِيُرِيَهُمَا سَوۡءَٰتِهِمَآۚ إِنَّهُۥ يَرَىٰكُمۡ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُۥ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَا تَرَوۡنَهُمۡۗ إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلشَّيَٰطِينَ أَوۡلِيَآءَ لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:27.en: O Children of Adam! Let not Satan seduce you as he caused your (first) parents to go forth from the Garden and tore off from them their robe (of innocence) that he might manifest their shame to them. Lo! he seeth you, he and his tribe, from whence ye see him not. Lo! We have made the devils protecting friends for those who believe not

71:5.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوۡتُ قَوۡمِي لَيۡلࣰ ا وَنَهَارࣰ ا
71:5.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! I have called unto my people night and day

71:6.ar: فَلَمۡ يَزِدۡهُمۡ دُعَآءِيٓ إِلَّا فِرَارࣰ ا
71:6.en: But all my calling doth but add to their repugnance

71:7.ar: وَإِنِّي كُلَّمَا دَعَوۡتُهُمۡ لِتَغۡفِرَ لَهُمۡ جَعَلُوٓاْ أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ فِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡشَوۡاْ ثِيَابَهُمۡ وَأَصَرُّواْ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ ٱسۡتِكۡبَارࣰ ا
71:7.en: And lo! whenever I call unto them that Thou mayst pardon them they thrust their fingers in their ears and cover themselves with their garments and persist (in their refusal) and magnify themselves in pride

71:8.en: And lo! I have called unto them aloud

71:9.ar: ثُمَّ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَنتُ لَهُمۡ وَأَسۡرَرۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِسۡرَارࣰ ا
71:9.en: And lo! I have made public proclamation unto them, and I have appealed to them in private

7:33.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ رَبِّيَ ٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ وَٱلۡإِثۡمَ وَٱلۡبَغۡيَ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَأَن تُشۡرِكُواْ بِٱللَّهِ مَا لَمۡ يُنَزِّلۡ بِهِۦ سُلۡطَٰنࣰ ا وَأَن تَقُولُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
7:33.en: Say: My Lord forbiddeth only indecencies, such of them as are apparent and such as are within, and sin and wrongful oppression, and that ye associate with Allah that for which no warrant hath been revealed, and that ye tell concerning Allah that which ye know not

16:98.ar: فَإِذَا قَرَأۡتَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ فَٱسۡتَعِذۡ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ

EDuJDoU2rq4.speaker_note: Single voice continuing his Sunday tafseer cluster; mentions growing up in Syria and his own role speaking from the minbar
EDuJDoU2rq4.title: Surat Al-Jinn, Part 1: Verses 1-10
EDuJDoU2rq4.one_line: Opening Al-Jinn: Iblis's story, the jinn who heard the Prophet after Ta'if, outcomes of da'wah belonging to Allah, and dismantling jinn superstition.
EDuJDoU2rq4.summary: He places Al-Jinn beside Surat Nuh as two opposite examples of representing Islam: Nuh did everything right and won few followers, while the Prophet, praying alone on his lowest night after Ta'if, won over a group of jinn without knowing they were there. The lesson is that the task is ours and the outcome is Allah's, and that da'wah happens mostly through character. To explain the jinn's words he tells the background story of Iblis: a pious jinn raised among the angels who refused to honour Adam, argued from his fiery origin, and was granted respite and access to whisper to humans. Before reciting, he attacks the superstition that surrounds jinn among Muslims, calling it an industry with money and a comforting excuse attached, which is harder to dislodge than a belief; anxiety, trauma and neglect get blamed on jinn. Going through verses 1 to 10, he explains the jinn's testimony: the Quran guides to what is beneficial, Allah has no partner, wife or child, and their foolish one had lied about Allah. He dwells on the gravity of speaking about Allah without knowledge, including his own fear of it, on how humans seeking refuge in jinn only made things worse, and on the jinn admitting they know nothing of the unseen.

outline.heading: The third cluster: what representing Islam requires
outline.gist: The cluster from Al-Mulk to Al-Mursalat is about representing Islam. Its first four surahs set the basic requirements of ethics, closeness to Allah and a code of conduct; the next two give contrasting examples of da'wah.

outline.heading: Nuh and the jinn: effort without outcome, outcome without effort
outline.gist: Nuh did everything by the book and won few followers, not even his wife and son; in Al-Jinn almost no effort was made and the outcome came. Side by side they teach that your mission is to do the task correctly, and the result was never your responsibility.

outline.heading: Who the jinn are: smokeless fire, older than us, free to choose
outline.gist: Our knowledge of the jinn is limited: they were made of smokeless fire long before humans and live in a realm we cannot fully access. Like humans, and unlike other creatures, they can disobey, which is why the two are called the thaqalan.

outline.heading: A pious jinn raised among the angels
outline.gist: Long ago the jinn spread corruption and shed blood, but one of them was so pious that Allah raised him to the ranks of the angels. When Allah told them Adam was coming, the angels asked why He would place on earth a creation that would corrupt and shed blood as the jinn had.

outline.heading: Creation beyond humans and jinn
outline.gist: We are told about humans and jinn because they are part of our story, not because they are all Allah created. There may be countless other creations, and it is unwise to limit His creativity to what we see; the Hereafter is where we get to learn the rest.

outline.heading: Prostration as honour, and what would you have done?
outline.gist: The prostration was figurative: acknowledging that Adam had higher status by Allah's choice. If you find yourself sympathising with Iblis, that is the point of the story: learn it so your ego never overrides divine wisdom.

outline.heading: 'I am better than him': merit or essence
outline.gist: Adam had not taken a breath, so Iblis could not argue from merit and argued from essence: fire against altered, foul-smelling mud, as gold is better than dirt.

outline.heading: Arrogant, or of the exalted? Iblis asks for respite
outline.gist: Allah asked whether he had become arrogant or thought himself superior by nature. He could answer neither, so he asked for time until the Day of Judgment to prove Adam unworthy.

outline.heading: Granted respite and access to whisper
outline.gist: Allah granted it, and Iblis vowed to lead Adam's descendants by the reins. To whisper across realms he and his followers were given access to us; we are weak and easily swayed, and he is not ignorant: he knows exactly what he did.

outline.heading: A knowing enemy who sees you unseen
outline.gist: Shaytan is our enemy, so take him as one; he has no interest in friendship, only in ruining us. He has studied human weakness since Adam and, with his tribe, sees us from where we cannot see him.

outline.heading: Changing a belief vs changing an industry
outline.gist: By the end of the surah it is clear exactly what jinn can and cannot do, so why the superstition? Because there is money in it: changing a belief is one thing, changing an industry another.

outline.heading: The Prophet was up against a system
outline.gist: He brought a simple, pure argument against incoherent claims, but he faced a way of life rooted in Makkah's politics and social structure, not a rational argument. Uprooting it nearly broke his back, which is why the old era is called Jahiliyyah, and much of that system has been brought back.

outline.heading: A weak challenger that still wins: blame, comfort and money
outline.gist: The argument against jinn superstition is easily won, yet people still say a jinn is in the house. It offers something to blame, pseudo-comfort that something was done, and an escape from asking whether we raised our children badly or someone is ill; exorcism is a multi-million-dollar industry Muslims have joined.

outline.heading: When it was revealed: the night after Ta'if
outline.gist: A Makkan surah, most likely from the tenth year, after the Prophet was humiliated at Ta'if and shut out of Makkah; some place it earlier, at a market. Asked by Aishah about his hardest day, he named that day, when he walked aimlessly until Qarn al-Tha'alib.

outline.heading: 'She has anxiety, not a jinn'
outline.gist: Nothing gets him dismissed more than telling a parent their daughter has anxiety, not a jinn. Even his educated parents in Syria once brought an old woman to pour melted lead into the corners of the house, and an unmarried 28-year-old is blamed on magic or the evil eye rather than his character.

outline.heading: Tajweed: a stopped noon with shaddah keeps two counts
outline.gist: Stopping on al-jinn, the noon with shaddah still gets its two counts of ghunnah, as in inna; the stop does not remove them.

outline.heading: Tajweed: the fading alif at verse endings
outline.gist: The verses end in an alif, which fades out over two counts. Do not chop it off as if cutting wood, which adds a hamza at the end.

outline.heading: 'Say: it has been revealed to me': a challenge to the status quo
outline.gist: When Allah tells the Prophet to say something, rather than addressing people directly, it challenges a norm people resist. That is why he had to keep saying it, as a mission of reform.

outline.heading: Nafar: a small group, on his lowest night
outline.gist: Nafar is a small, countable group, roughly three to ten. They heard him on the night returning from Ta'if, the lowest moment of his life as he felt it.

outline.heading: A Prophet who always had a plan, and the night he had none
outline.gist: He always worked with a plan and adjusted it when things changed, but that night he felt lost: shut out of Makkah, responsible for young Zayd, his daughters alone at home, Khadijah and Abu Talib gone. He camped in the valley and spent the night in prayer.

outline.heading: A Prophet to humans and jinn
outline.gist: He was sent to both; the jinn will have no prophet after him, though most scholars think they had prophets before. They had been told to listen to him when he came, and were sent his way that night.

outline.heading: They watched his character, then heard his prayer
outline.gist: They had watched how Ta'if treated him, how he cared for and fed Zayd, then heard him stand in prayer. He had no idea they were there, which is why it had to be revealed to him.

outline.heading: Quran: recitable, structured speech
outline.gist: The word Quran means words that can be recited, with rhythm and organisation, coming in structured units with a beginning and an end: surahs.

outline.heading: It guides to rushd: always what benefits you
outline.gist: Rushd is everything truly beneficial, more than righteousness, as in the dua asking to always make the decision that is best for you. Following the Quran can never lead you to harm.

outline.heading: Exalted is the jadd of our Lord: no wife, no child
outline.gist: The jinn vow never again to associate anyone with their Lord. Jadd means status, which is why a grandfather is called jadd: the father of the father whom everyone serves. Our Lord's status is high above taking a wife or a child.

outline.heading: 'Our foolish one': Iblis's false grievance
outline.gist: This is why he told the background story: Iblis rallied the jinn with a tale that Adam stole their rank and that Allah was unjust. Not all jinn are enemies; these are our brothers working toward the same goals, unseen.

outline.heading: Nuh by the book; the Prophet unaware he was giving da'wah
outline.gist: Nuh called his people night and day, publicly and privately, and got few believers. The Prophet was only praying and being himself, yet the jinn came to believe in large numbers.

outline.heading: Represent the message; the results are His
outline.gist: Your job is to represent, teach and practise the message as it should be. You may labour like Nuh for little, or say something you forget that benefits people you never learn about until Allah reveals it.

outline.heading: Safih: a category in Islamic law
outline.gist: Safih is the person not competent to manage his affairs. In Islamic law it is a category, not an insult: people with addictions or certain disabilities are protected from themselves so they do not ruin themselves and burden society.

outline.heading: Shatat: far off the road
outline.gist: The jinn use the word linguistically for the one who lied to them. Shatat is going far off the road, as far as the shore is from any road; what Iblis taught surely included shirk and the claim of a wife and child, along with his grievance against Adam.

outline.heading: Wa anna: listening to the jinn's own conversation
outline.gist: This is the one place in the Quran where you hear jinn speak at length. Each verse opens with wa anna because the Prophet is relaying, point by point, what they said among themselves.

outline.heading: 'We never thought anyone would lie about Allah'
outline.gist: Having declared their belief, they explain why they were misled: they assumed no human or jinn would dare lie in Allah's name. It shows how pure these souls were.

outline.heading: Lying about the Prophet: a mutawatir warning
outline.gist: The hadith that whoever lies about the Prophet should take his seat in the Fire reached us through so many chains that it is as certain as the Quran.

outline.heading: Saying about Allah what you do not know
outline.gist: When Allah gathers the categories of the forbidden in one verse, the last is saying in His name what you have no knowledge of. It is the most dangerous thing in the world.

outline.heading: His own fear of speaking in Allah's name
outline.gist: He only does it, he says, because he started young and ambitious; every sheikh he had told him to stay on the sidelines. One misinterpretation or agenda slipped in, and how would he defend himself before Allah?

outline.heading: Lies that rally people to kill
outline.gist: The jinn could not imagine anyone starting a cult, promising Paradise for obedience, and sending people to murder, burn and bomb in God's name.

outline.heading: Pure souls, and the preacher's temptation to sell out
outline.gist: Selling out God for money, status or a politician's approval is a problem of our time. Becoming popular is easy if you say what people want to hear; the fear is saying what you know Allah did not mean because it is popular or your job is at risk.

outline.heading: Humans sought refuge in jinn
outline.gist: Many humans sought refuge in the jinn, which made the jinn feel important and powerful. Every culture has tried to get the spirits on its side, under one name or another.

outline.heading: Rahaq: more fatigue and humiliation
outline.gist: Rahaq is fatigue and humiliation: the refuge-seeking only made humans' state worse. People have always looked to the metaphysical for answers because it is more exciting.

outline.heading: Why run the risk? Superstition we deny but obey
outline.gist: People who say they do not believe will still refuse to enter a place said to have jinn, just in case. Either you have a clear belief system or you do not; the superstition is embedded in the culture.

outline.heading: Isti'adhah: fear of the unknown belongs to Allah
outline.gist: Seeking refuge is an act, which is why recitation begins with it. Fear comes from not knowing the future; if you knew exactly what was coming you would not fear it. So people seek safety in something, and Allah teaches us to seek it in no one but Him.

outline.heading: How human fear fed Shaytan's narrative
outline.gist: Watching humans seek refuge in creatures weaker than themselves, again and again, made the jinn think Iblis was right that humans did not deserve the rank Allah gave them.

outline.heading: They thought Allah would never resurrect anyone
outline.gist: Some read ba'th here as sending a messenger; he prefers resurrection, humanity's oldest question, which includes accountability and reward or punishment. Like many people, they thought this life was all there is.

outline.heading: Tajweed: keeping adjacent letters steady
outline.gist: Recapping the jinn's account so far, he recites on and explains how to pronounce two adjacent letters cleanly, without a small jump, when stopping.

outline.heading: Leave the weak narrations about jinn
outline.gist: There are narrations about jinn that lack authenticity and clarity, and most scholars leave them alone. We know only that jinn exist differently and can approach the heavens, which is how Iblis came to be among the angels.

outline.heading: The sky newly filled with stern guards and shooting stars
outline.gist: Mula'at describes an act of filling that had not happened before: suddenly the sky was packed with stern guards and shuhub, falling stars or comets.

outline.heading: Seats for listening, now a flame lying in wait
outline.gist: They used to sit in places in the sky to overhear; now whoever tries finds a shihab waiting for him. Rasad is something blocking your way that will take you down if you cross the line.

outline.heading: 'We do not know': the jinn admit they know nothing of the future
outline.gist: The discussion is closed: they cannot hear anything or bring any information, and they do not know whether evil or good is intended for the people of earth. We are hearing this from the jinn themselves.

outline.heading: Yet the village healer knows?
outline.gist: The jinn know nothing, but the old man with his remedies of goat hair boiled in goose urine supposedly does. Perhaps the person is ill, traumatised, abused or neglected and needs a health care professional.

outline.heading: Al-an: barred as of now
outline.gist: Al-an, 'now', is rare in the Quran and marks the present tense precisely: as of now, anyone who tries to listen meets a burning flame. He calls the surah beautiful, a chance to hear other creatures accept Islam, and asks everyone to read the rest and reflect.

Stop blaming jinn for anxiety, illness or family problems; seek proper care and own the responsibility
Seek refuge and comfort only in Allah, not in healers, charms or spirits
Never attribute anything to Allah without knowledge
Read the rest of Surat Al-Jinn at home and reflect on it

72:11.ar: وَأَنَّا مِنَّا ٱلصَّٰلِحُونَ وَمِنَّا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَۖ كُنَّا طَرَآئِقَ قِدَدࣰ ا
72:11.en: And among us there are righteous folk and among us there are far from that. We are sects having different rules

72:12.ar: وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن نُّعۡجِزَ ٱللَّهَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَن نُّعۡجِزَهُۥ هَرَبࣰ ا
72:12.en: And we know that we cannot escape from Allah in the earth, nor can we escape by flight

72:13.ar: وَأَنَّا لَمَّا سَمِعۡنَا ٱلۡهُدَىٰٓ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦۖ فَمَن يُؤۡمِنۢ بِرَبِّهِۦ فَلَا يَخَافُ بَخۡسࣰ ا وَلَا رَهَقࣰ ا
72:13.en: And when we heard the guidance, we believed therein, and whoso believeth in his Lord, he feareth neither loss nor oppression

72:14.ar: وَأَنَّا مِنَّا ٱلۡمُسۡلِمُونَ وَمِنَّا ٱلۡقَٰسِطُونَۖ فَمَنۡ أَسۡلَمَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ تَحَرَّوۡاْ رَشَدࣰ ا
72:14.en: And there are among us some who have surrendered (to Allah) and there are among us some who are unjust. And whoso hath surrendered to Allah, such have taken the right path purposefully

72:15.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلۡقَٰسِطُونَ فَكَانُواْ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَبࣰ ا
72:15.en: And as for those who are unjust, they are firewood for hell

72:1.ar: قُلۡ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسۡتَمَعَ نَفَرࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا سَمِعۡنَا قُرۡءَانًا عَجَبࣰ ا
72:1.en: Say (O Muhammad): It is revealed unto me that a company of the Jinn gave ear, and they said: Lo! we have heard a marvellous Qur'an

72:2.ar: يَهۡدِيٓ إِلَى ٱلرُّشۡدِ فَـَٔامَنَّا بِهِۦۖ وَلَن نُّشۡرِكَ بِرَبِّنَآ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:2.en: Which guideth unto righteousness, so we believe in it and we ascribe no partner unto our Lord

72:3.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ تَعَٰلَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا مَا ٱتَّخَذَ صَٰحِبَةࣰ وَلَا وَلَدࣰ ا
72:3.en: And (we believe) that He - exalted be the glory of our Lord! - hath taken neither wife nor son

72:4.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ كَانَ يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنَا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ شَطَطࣰ ا
72:4.en: And that the foolish one among us used to speak concerning Allah an atrocious lie

72:5.ar: وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن تَقُولَ ٱلۡإِنسُ وَٱلۡجِنُّ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبࣰ ا
72:5.en: And lo! we had supposed that humankind and jinn would not speak a lie concerning Allah

72:6.ar: وَأَنَّهُۥ كَانَ رِجَالࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡإِنسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجَالࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ فَزَادُوهُمۡ رَهَقࣰ ا
72:6.en: And indeed (O Muhammad) individuals of humankind used to invoke the protection of individuals of the jinn, so that they increased them in revolt against Allah

72:7.ar: وَأَنَّهُمۡ ظَنُّواْ كَمَا ظَنَنتُمۡ أَن لَّن يَبۡعَثَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:7.en: And indeed they supposed, even as ye suppose, that Allah would not raise anyone (from the dead)

72:8.ar: وَأَنَّا لَمَسۡنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ فَوَجَدۡنَٰهَا مُلِئَتۡ حَرَسࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ ا وَشُهُبࣰ ا
72:8.en: And (the Jinn who had listened to the Qur'an said): We had sought the heaven but had found it filled with strong warders and meteors

72:9.ar: وَأَنَّا كُنَّا نَقۡعُدُ مِنۡهَا مَقَٰعِدَ لِلسَّمۡعِۖ فَمَن يَسۡتَمِعِ ٱلۡأٓنَ يَجِدۡ لَهُۥ شِهَابࣰ ا رَّصَدࣰ ا
72:9.en: And we used to sit on places (high) therein to listen. But he who listeneth now findeth a flame in wait for him

72:10.ar: وَأَنَّا لَا نَدۡرِيٓ أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَمۡ أَرَادَ بِهِمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ رَشَدࣰ ا
72:10.en: And we know not whether harm is boded unto all who are in the earth, or whether their Lord intendeth guidance for them

39:3.ar: أَلَا لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡخَالِصُۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَ مَا نَعۡبُدُهُمۡ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ زُلۡفَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحۡكُمُ بَيۡنَهُمۡ فِي مَا هُمۡ فِيهِ يَخۡتَلِفُونَۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي مَنۡ هُوَ كَٰذِبࣱ كَفَّارࣱ‏
39:3.en: Surely pure religion is for Allah only. And those who choose protecting friends beside Him (say): We worship them only that they may bring us near unto Allah. Lo! Allah will judge between them concerning that wherein they differ. Lo! Allah guideth not him who is a liar, an ingrate

34:14.ar: فَلَمَّا قَضَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ مَا دَلَّهُمۡ عَلَىٰ مَوۡتِهِۦٓ إِلَّا دَآبَّةُ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ تَأۡكُلُ مِنسَأَتَهُۥۖ فَلَمَّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ ٱلۡجِنُّ أَن لَّوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ ٱلۡغَيۡبَ مَا لَبِثُواْ فِي ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡمُهِينِ
34:14.en: And when We decreed death for him, nothing showed his death to them save a creeping creature of the earth which gnawed away his staff. And when he fell the jinn saw clearly how, if they had known the Unseen, they would not have continued in despised toil

7:116.ar: قَالَ أَلۡقُواْۖ فَلَمَّآ أَلۡقَوۡاْ سَحَرُوٓاْ أَعۡيُنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱسۡتَرۡهَبُوهُمۡ وَجَآءُو بِسِحۡرٍ عَظِيمࣲ‏
7:116.en: He said: Throw! And when they threw they cast a spell upon the people's eyes, and overawed them, and produced a mighty spell

25:8.ar: أَوۡ يُلۡقَىٰٓ إِلَيۡهِ كَنزٌ أَوۡ تَكُونُ لَهُۥ جَنَّةࣱ يَأۡكُلُ مِنۡهَاۚ وَقَالَ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ إِن تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا رَجُلࣰ ا مَّسۡحُورًا
25:8.en: Or (why is not) treasure thrown down unto him, or why hath he not a paradise from whence to eat? And the evil-doers say: Ye are but following a man bewitched

4:76.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱلطَّٰغُوتِ فَقَٰتِلُوٓاْ أَوۡلِيَآءَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۖ إِنَّ كَيۡدَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ كَانَ ضَعِيفًا
4:76.en: Those who believe do battle for the cause of Allah; and those who disbelieve do battle for the cause of idols. So fight the minions of the devil. Lo! the devil's strategy is ever weak

10:107.ar: وَإِن يَمۡسَسۡكَ ٱللَّهُ بِضُرࣲّ فَلَا كَاشِفَ لَهُۥٓ إِلَّا هُوَۖ وَإِن يُرِدۡكَ بِخَيۡرࣲ فَلَا رَآدَّ لِفَضۡلِهِۦۚ يُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
10:107.en: If Allah afflicteth thee with some hurt, there is none who can remove it save Him; and if He desireth good for thee, there is none who can repel His bounty. He striketh with it whom He will of his bondmen. He is the Forgiving, the Merciful

29:14.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمۡ أَلۡفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمۡسِينَ عَامࣰ ا فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلطُّوفَانُ وَهُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ
29:14.en: And verily we sent Noah (as Our messenger) unto his folk, and he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years; and the flood engulfed them, for they were wrong-doers

49:13.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرࣲ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ شُعُوبࣰ ا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَىٰكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
49:13.en: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware

1MSBroKipDQ.speaker: adnan
1MSBroKipDQ.speaker_note: Single voice continuing his Al-Jinn series; mentions his 12 years in the community, his son and his Syrian village
1MSBroKipDQ.title: Surat Al-Jinn, Part 2: Verses 11-15
1MSBroKipDQ.one_line: Jinn superstition as a symptom of Muslim de-education, then the jinn's honest account of their past and their split into Muslims and the unjust.
1MSBroKipDQ.summary: He opens by framing Muslims as coming out of a 300-year slump of de-education, in which superstition has crept back and now claims religious backing. The pre-Islamic Arabs ran wars on divining arrows; the Prophet replaced this with critical thinking. Using the jinn's own admission that they know nothing of the unseen, and Sulayman's death on his staff, he argues that jinn can only whisper; possession, exorcism and much of what is called sihr have no authentic basis and were borrowed from other traditions centuries later. These labels harm the mentally ill, give people something to blame instead of taking responsibility, and leave no room for Allah's decree. The prophetic remedy is reciting Quran over yourself and your family and not flaunting blessings before those who lack them. Turning to verses 11 to 15, he admires how the jinn calmly explain why they had been misled and what changed, and notes that their struggle was never doubting God, while ours is certainty. He asks listeners, especially parents worried about youth leaving Islam, to do the same exercise: name what held them back, what the Quran changed for them, and the blind spots it came to fix, above all hidden racism.

outline.heading: A 300-year slump: less educated than a thousand years ago
outline.gist: Muslims are coming off three centuries of losses and systemic de-education. Muslim lands were more educated, more scientific and more law-abiding a thousand years ago than today, a rare historical finding.

outline.heading: Rebuilding minds: the Prophet's transformation of a generation
outline.gist: What takes an hour to destroy takes a month to rebuild, and minds take far longer than concrete. The change in people's thinking, ethics and maturity before and after the Prophet is plain to see; how he achieved it deserves study.

outline.heading: Diagnosing where we regressed
outline.gist: It takes little to slide back to the ways of Jahiliyyah, and there is no awakening without diagnosing where we did. Superstition is one front, and it has gone far beyond bearable.

outline.heading: Superstition blamed on Islam: the worst case
outline.gist: Superstition recognised as wrong is one thing; superstition with a backbone in faith is the worst, like political, financial or domestic misconduct blamed on Islam. Prophets came for reform, and an ummah whose first command was to read sliding into superstition is depressing.

outline.heading: Pre-Islamic Arabs: omens, winds and divining arrows
outline.gist: The Arabs were intelligent but read meaning into animals, scents, winds and clouds, and drew marked arrows from a sack before big decisions, even wars. The Prophet instilled critical thinking and removed these superstitions.

outline.heading: Shirk as superstition, and its revival
outline.gist: Shirk rests on fear that a rock can harm or help you, so people pay their respects just in case; idol worshippers said they knew Allah was supreme and the idols only brought them closer. These ideas are now revived in Islam's name through outdated or mistaken fatwas.

outline.heading: The jinn's own admission: struck down, knowing nothing
outline.gist: In last week's verses the jinn found the sky full of guards and flames, are struck if they try to listen, and do not know whether evil or good is intended for the people of earth. The Quran repeats the point.

outline.heading: Sulayman's death on his staff
outline.gist: Only Sulayman and Dawud could command the jinn. When Sulayman died leaning on his staff, the jinn kept working in fear until termites ate through it and he fell; had they known the unseen, they would not have toiled for nothing.

outline.heading: Whispering, not possession
outline.gist: Waswasah is the extent of the jinn's power; it can be bothersome, but they cannot take the driver's seat. Possession and exorcism come from Catholic and earlier Jewish tradition and entered Muslim life about three centuries after the Prophet.

outline.heading: Quranic sihr: fooling the eyes
outline.gist: Sihr in the Quran is illusion, which is how Pharaoh's magicians differed from Musa, whose staff became a real snake. What exactly it referred to is unclear, and there is no evidence it extends to today.

outline.heading: The claim that the Prophet was bewitched
outline.gist: The Quran rejects the disbelievers' charge that the Prophet was bewitched, yet some re-established it; such narrations have problems in chain and wording. There is no authentic evidence for possession or for magic affecting people.

outline.heading: Jinn, sihr and the eye: from belief to pseudo-science
outline.gist: These three, with conspiracies, account for half of Muslims' problems. He is not denying they exist, but rejecting the claim to diagnose, treat and cure them, and to profit from it.

outline.heading: Telling a schizophrenic he has a jinn
outline.gist: It gives an already paranoid person an idea no psychiatrist can disprove, since nothing can be scanned or shown; it butchers him. When he asked for the criteria behind such diagnoses, he got made-up rubbish.

outline.heading: If it were real, the Prophet would have taught it
outline.gist: He taught ruqyah, recitation and dua, and warned against flaunting a good life before people who are struggling.

outline.heading: It's hasad, just not the way you think
outline.gist: A young man blames envy for a failed proposal, and he is right: a rival told the bride's father something damaging. Envy works through people's actions, not laser eyes.

outline.heading: Needing a hanger to blame, which ends up blaming God
outline.gist: Without critical thinking people skip cause and effect and want an external culprit, which feels wonderful and spares them accountability and change. But who is really being blamed? In the end, Allah.

outline.heading: The further from the deen, the more superstitious
outline.gist: Superstition runs through Muslim culture and is strongest among those far from the masjid and from learning. Those who come closer learn how small a space these topics have in Islam.

outline.heading: Left with our own choices: a symptom of long ignorance
outline.gist: Whatever information jinn once brought ended with the Prophet, as these verses state, leaving us with our own decisions, which is harder. Seeing these beliefs as symptoms of prolonged ignorance, not a reason to call people ignorant, shows how to change them.

outline.heading: Do ruqyah yourself, every day
outline.gist: The cure is study of the Quran and Sunnah: recite the Quran daily and do ruqyah over yourself and your loved ones. Ruqyah is the request he gets most, yet neither the Prophet nor Abu Bakr spent their time doing it for everyone.

outline.heading: The sheikh possesses nothing
outline.gist: The model of a holy man with special powers is inherited from Catholicism. He has no more ability to help than anyone else; a family member who loves the person should recite, not an awkward stranger brought from the masjid.

outline.heading: Absent from the Prophet's life, prevalent after the third century
outline.gist: He studied the subject for years, ready to accept whatever Allah taught, and found less and less emphasis on it the closer he looked. The stories spread after the third century; earlier scholars reflected their times, but today it cannot be accepted.

outline.heading: A religious diagnosis needs a religious prescription
outline.gist: Labelling marital problems or mental health struggles this way makes them incurable. If you call it possession, show the treatment plan clearly described in the Quran or Sunnah; you cannot make it up.

outline.heading: Copycat exorcisms, and the harm he has seen
outline.gist: Practitioners copy exorcisms from centuries when Muslims were translating the world's sciences and Europeans were doing exorcisms; now the roles are reversed. He has seen this thinking harm more people than any other, and once parents arrive sure there is a jinn, he can do little.

outline.heading: Easy to win on evidence, impossible socially
outline.gist: Islamically the case is easy and opponents' evidence is weak, but people who have accepted a belief look for anything to strengthen it. Shaytan's plot is weak and he can only whisper; why give him more power than Allah did?

outline.heading: A village overrun by jinn
outline.gist: In his Syrian village it seemed every second household had a jinn; a mother blamed sihr for her son's failure to marry when his manners and hygiene explained it. An external cause is easier to accept than an internal one.

outline.heading: Where is Allah's decree?
outline.gist: If every hardship is blamed on jinn, sihr or the eye, there is no room for qadar, which includes difficulty. If all people gathered to harm you, they could harm you only with what Allah decreed, and no one can lift a hardship He sends.

outline.heading: The prophetic prescription: recite, and do not flaunt
outline.gist: Recite Quran at home and over your children as they sleep, and do not show off blessings to those without them unless you are generous with them. You are responsible not to envy, and also not to provoke envy.

outline.heading: Recap: da'wah through character and the jinn's testimony
outline.gist: The Prophet won jinn without knowing it, while Nuh spent 950 years for few believers: different outcomes, not different worth. He reviews what the jinn said so far, including that the sky could once be overheard and now cannot.

outline.heading: Some righteous, some less: tara'iq qidada
outline.gist: Before the Quran there were pious jinn and others less so, walking separate paths. Tara'iq is the plural of tariqah, a way, and qidad are narrow strips, like strips of dried meat.

outline.heading: We knew we could not escape Allah
outline.gist: They knew they could neither defeat Allah on earth nor flee from Him. Along with trusting liars, being flattered by human refuge-seeking and doubting resurrection, which means doubting accountability, this was their state before.

outline.heading: Their struggle was never God; ours is certainty
outline.gist: Humans have always struggled with certainty in Allah and His attributes, then accountability. The jinn's points show their obstacle was different: they knew Him.

outline.heading: We misled them too
outline.gist: By always seeking refuge in jinn, humans made them feel more powerful than they were. They whisper and we reciprocate with superstition, which is why the Quran speaks of jinn and humans together.

outline.heading: Weak eman will fail you
outline.gist: Jinn struggle with shirk, resurrection and Allah's attributes, not with God Himself; most humans do struggle with Him. If you have doubts, deal with them, because weak faith fails you eventually.

outline.heading: Unanalysed faith inherits garbage
outline.gist: Build your conclusions on facts. A faith never examined is full of inherited superstitions; a half-examined one is full of doubts. Both are hard to help.

outline.heading: The companions examined everything; Umar's six years
outline.gist: The first generation was special because the Prophet knocked down every norm intellectually first, so they had to admit their wrongs and test the new teaching. Umar took six years, yet stands right behind Abu Bakr, because once convinced he committed wholeheartedly.

outline.heading: Say what the jinn said: name your obstacles
outline.gist: He wants a generation willing to say: here is what I heard, what I know now, and why I did not follow it before. What keeps you from being a proud, practising Muslim? Talk about it openly, not to confess sins but to find solutions.

outline.heading: Our children's struggles are new to us
outline.gist: The next generation faces struggles we may not understand, and some old ways of thinking may no longer work. What should we emphasise for youth, and what can we let go?

outline.heading: Social image and youth leaving Islam
outline.gist: Parents still care more about how their children look to peers than about the basics. Almost weekly, in twelve years here, he speaks with a parent whose child has left Islam; some return having lost much ground, many driven away by false beliefs and misplaced emphasis.

outline.heading: Wa anna: recalling honestly
outline.gist: Each verse opens with wa anna, like someone recalling one thing after another: we used to listen, some of us were good, we walked different paths. He loves their honesty and purity, which is what we need.

outline.heading: Explaining your reasons is not making excuses
outline.gist: A pure soul can say what it did for twenty years, why, and that it did not work. Stating the reasoning helps others recognise their own and change it.

outline.heading: A unique surah: meet the Quran as they did
outline.gist: No surah is put together like it, and students often fail when memorizing it. Listen to what the jinn say and mimic their experience: hear it, accept it, and never again think ill of your Lord.

outline.heading: No fear of bakhs or rahaq
outline.gist: Having heard the guidance and believed, whoever believes in his Lord fears neither bakhs, being given less than his due, nor rahaq, humiliation he cannot defend himself against.

outline.heading: Now only two groups: muslimun and qasitun
outline.gist: Before, the jinn followed many paths; after hearing the Quran there are two. A qasit, unlike a muqsit, swerves from what he knows is fair; in Arabic one derivation can give a word's meaning and another its opposite.

outline.heading: Why qasitun: the message reached them at once
outline.gist: The term fits the jinn's experience. Unlike us, they seem able to spread a message quickly among themselves, so every jinn was put before a choice.

outline.heading: Refusing Adam's rank: pride and racism
outline.gist: Those who submit accept that Iblis was wrong and Adam's rank is Allah's will. The qasitun keep Iblis's legacy out of what they call integrity, really arrogance and racism; they had been told lies that made Allah seem flawed, and some refused even after the Quran corrected them.

outline.heading: Those who submit sought the right course
outline.gist: Taharraw rashada: they searched out the path truly in their best interest, rushd as he explained at the start of the surah.

outline.heading: Fuel for Hell, chosen knowingly
outline.gist: Most people who were truly certain of Hell would not live toward it; our problem is certainty. These jinn know it is there and prefer it to submitting, a choice we do not understand.

outline.heading: What has the Quran changed in you?

Hd6-cN6_9g8.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Honesty, Episode 8
Hd6-cN6_9g8.one_line: What the Quran and sunnah say about truthfulness, how to filter feedback, and the Prophet as the model of honesty with oneself.
Hd6-cN6_9g8.summary: The sheikh reminds his students that honesty has three dimensions: with people, with Allah and with oneself, and that the last two matter most. He goes through the hadith that truthfulness leads to righteousness and Paradise until a person is recorded as a siddiq, the rank just below prophethood, and the narration that a believer may fall into many sins but not lying, since lying is a way of life, not a single slip. Because self-honesty has no outside reviewer, he returns to asking friends for feedback, then describes self-honesty as a filtering system: neither swatting away every criticism nor being crushed by it, like small steering corrections on a straight road. Humans have insight into themselves, and the inner voice still knows. Self-deception hardens with age, which is why conversion takes radical self-honesty that Muslims must also live. The Prophet was the same person in poverty and in power because he had leveled with himself, never complained despite many losses, and rebuked Umar's worry about worldly comfort. He closes by asking students to accept responsibility rather than blame the divine, grow through friction, and reconnect with the raw self that enjoys simple things.

outline.heading: Opening
Three dimensions of honesty
outline.gist: Honesty with people is the familiar one, but honesty with Allah and with oneself matter more, and outer lying is a symptom.

outline.heading: Truthfulness leads to righteousness
outline.gist: The hadith that sidq leads to birr and birr to Paradise; a person keeps seeking truthfulness until recorded as a siddiq.

outline.heading: The rank of the siddiq
outline.gist: Being a siddiq is the highest rank a person can choose, just below prophethood and above martyrdom.

outline.heading: Lying leads to wickedness
outline.gist: The other half of the hadith: lying leads to fujur and the Fire until a person is recorded as a liar.

outline.heading: A believer sins but does not lie
outline.gist: A believer may commit many sins but not lying, because lying is a way of life that breeds more lies like dominoes.

outline.heading: Untangling years of woven lies
outline.gist: Self-honesty takes long because we must trace back where we began lying to ourselves.

outline.heading: Truthfulness with Allah in the Quran
outline.gist: Verses on a footing of truth with their Lord, a seat of truth near the King, and entering and leaving truthfully; scholars rank honesty first among ethics.

outline.heading: No outside reviewer for self-honesty
outline.gist: Muraqabah and muhasabah keep self-honesty in check; asking a friend is the closest thing to outside feedback.

outline.heading: What a friend's feedback reveals
outline.gist: If you missed how someone who loves you experiences your shared friendship, ask what else you have missed.

outline.heading: Swatting away versus being crushed
outline.gist: Some reject all criticism and some are destroyed by it; self-honesty balances self-criticism with confidence and filters feedback.

outline.heading: Steering on a straight road
outline.gist: Staying on course needs small responses to the terrain, neither rigid nor overreacting, from an honest baseline.

outline.heading: The human being has insight into himself
outline.gist: Reasons differ from excuses; we know inwardly whether we are lying, which is why polygraphs work.

outline.heading: You cannot convince Allah
outline.gist: On the Day of Judgment the lie will be traced back; admitting the truth now brings humility and seeking forgiveness.

outline.heading: Self-deception hardens with age
outline.gist: Young people can drop their masks quickly; by sixty narratives are so set that arguing is pointless.

outline.heading: Conversion demands self-honesty
outline.gist: Accepting Islam means admitting one's life rested on error; Muslims who expect this of others must live it themselves.

outline.heading: The Prophet's honesty with himself
outline.gist: Despite an orphaned, hardworking life of care for others, he admitted something was missing and sought it in the cave.

outline.heading: The same man at the bottom and the top
outline.gist: Insults and adoration did not change him because nothing people said told him anything about himself he did not know.

outline.heading: Self-honesty is a way of life
outline.gist: It is not an achievement but constant self-criticism balanced by confidence.

outline.heading: Take something from every piece of feedback
outline.gist: His teacher told him to start speaking to children and to learn something from every critique, including being called a machine gun.

outline.heading: You only grow from friction
outline.gist: Tough supervisors, stressful days and volunteering to be wrong are where growth happens.

outline.heading: Turn your critical eye on yourself
outline.gist: We easily diagnose everyone else; use that faculty on yourself, as the Prophet never complained or blamed others.

outline.heading: The Prophet's many losses
outline.gist: Around nineteen close family and friends died in his lifetime, yet he did not complain.

outline.heading: Umar in the Prophet's upper room
outline.gist: Seeing the Prophet's bare storeroom and mat marks, Umar asked how long they would live poor, and was rebuked for that concern.

outline.heading: Either your responsibility or Allah's decree
outline.gist: Blaming circumstances is blaming the divine; except in rare cases like genetic illness, find your own share of responsibility.

outline.heading: The raw self and lost joy
outline.gist: Removing the roles reveals a consciousness that can find harmony; addictions arise when people can no longer find joy.

outline.heading: Simple joys and the Quran's signs
outline.gist: His four-year-old content with sand and water; the Quran repeatedly points us to the sun, rivers and rain to enjoy and know Allah.

outline.heading: Raw love and peeling off the masks
outline.gist: Love that needs accessories fades; knowing your raw self lets you weigh any feedback calmly.

outline.heading: Outro
