Xjm4zJ7Nigk.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Knowledge to Attitudes
Xjm4zJ7Nigk.one_line: The series' umbrella point: knowledge that does not become attitude and behaviour is useless and even testifies against you.
Xjm4zJ7Nigk.summary: Second episode of 'Achieving the Outcomes', setting out what he calls the umbrella point of the series: knowledge must turn into attitude. He starts from At-Tawbah 9:34-35, where the learned men of earlier nations consumed people's wealth unjustly despite knowing better, cited not to disparage them but as a warning. Three hadith follow: the worst of people is the immoral man who reads the Book and follows none of it; knowledge in the heart benefits while knowledge on the tongue testifies against you; and the scholar, reciter, martyr and philanthropist who acted for secondary gain are the first fuel of Hell. Knowing halal and haram or the Prophet's conduct with his family means nothing if you abuse yours. True knowledge humbles and produces reverence (Fatir 35:28); knowledge that is not lived backfires, yet ignorance is worse and inexcusable. People learned from the Prophet and the Sahabah because the knowledge visibly transformed them, so do not learn from those it has not changed. The world now runs on the law of the strong; a Muslim with knowledge refuses to join it and must not oppress when he gains strength. Students should spend the summer learning real things, as he did. Muslims talk big and argue well, but the four imams were followed for how they lived, not for the information they held.

outline.heading: Opening
At-Tawbah: the learned who consumed people's wealth
outline.gist: Many scholars of earlier nations took people's wealth unjustly, hoarded it and will be branded with it. The Quran recounts this so Muslims avoid the same mistake, not to badmouth them.

outline.heading: Knowledge must become attitude
outline.gist: Those scholars knew better and consciously chose not to act. The series' first point: to achieve the outcomes, knowledge must translate into attitude, or it becomes a problem for you.

outline.heading: Students: spend the summer learning
outline.gist: School forces textbooks you still need, but the two summer months are for learning things that matter and building skills. Most of what he learned came in summers, with scholars and alongside physicians, pharmacists, engineers and lawyers at work; the mind is a sponge for only about a decade.

outline.heading: Tabuk: the best and the worst of people
outline.gist: Reclining on a palm tree in the year of Tabuk, the Prophet said the best of people works in Allah's way until death comes.

outline.heading: Two kinds of knowledge: heart and tongue
outline.gist: The worst is an ill-mannered man who reads the Book and follows none of it, knowledge only in the voice box. Knowledge in the heart turns into behaviour and benefits; knowledge on the tongue is evidence against you.

outline.heading: The first fuel of Hell
outline.gist: The scariest hadith to him: the scholar, the reciter, the one killed in battle and the philanthropist who sought secondary gain are the first Hell is kindled with. When he once taught it as his own view he was shot down; said in the Prophet's name, everyone listens.

outline.heading: Muslim by claim or by evidence
outline.gist: Knowing the Quran, halal and haram and what Allah loves means nothing unless it shows in how you live. Saying you are Muslim is one thing; being Muslim as evident in your life is another.

outline.heading: Knowing his conduct, then abusing your family
outline.gist: If you believe in compassion, order, human rights and justice but your life does not show it, what has knowledge done? You read how the Prophet treated his wife and children, then go home and abuse yours.

outline.heading: The more you know, the more you know your ignorance
outline.gist: Muslims who know they must respect neighbours, family and parents are often the loudest and most obnoxious. Real knowledge reveals your ignorance and humbles you: only the knowledgeable truly revere Allah.

outline.heading: Knowledge is reverence, not memorisation
outline.gist: Commenting on that verse, a companion said knowledge is not how many hadith or verses you have memorised but the reverence it produces in how you live. Unlived knowledge backfires.

outline.heading: Ignorance is worse, so learn and live it
outline.gist: Choosing not to learn backfires even more: ignorance is inexcusable. Young people must incorporate the profound teachings of the Quran into how they live.

outline.heading: Lower the gaze; fear no one but Allah
outline.gist: You cannot know the verse commanding believers to lower their gaze and guard their chastity and change nothing. If you know there is one God, how can fear of anyone else outrank fear of Him?

outline.heading: Learn from those whose knowledge changed them
outline.gist: Do not take knowledge from people it has not changed. People went to the Prophet because they saw its effect on him, then saw the companions turn from rough men into people who followed truth, wept at night and showed mercy to animals.

outline.heading: A world ruled by the law of the strong
outline.gist: Today there is no ethical standard, only whatever the one with the bigger bombs and army wants: the law of the jungle. A Muslim who knows Allah's commands refuses to join or strengthen it, and must not oppress the moment he gains strength.

outline.heading: The umbrella topic: the one book with no falsehood
outline.gist: This is the topic everything else in the series fits under. Every textbook has errors to filter; the Quran has none, so what remains is turning it into attitude, which is why the Prophet's hadith on knowledge backfiring are so harsh.

outline.heading: Interlude
Would anyone listen to a rude scholar?
outline.gist: Knowledge has to turn into attitude. If he knew all this but was mean, rude, oppressive and without compassion in every interaction, would anyone listen to him?

outline.heading: A bare minimum: we talk the talk
outline.gist: He is not perfect, but there is a bare minimum to hold yourself to from the book you claim to know. Muslims argue brilliantly and with certainty for hours; show some of it in behaviour.

outline.heading: The four imams were followed for how they lived

Y24DnM_zmno.one_line: Summary of the self-honesty module: three dualities, the raw self beneath the roles, and the tools of muraqabah and muhasabah.
Y24DnM_zmno.summary: Closing the self-honesty module, the sheikh restates that honesty with oneself is the highest form of honesty and one of the four principles of tazkiyah. It shows most in disputes, where people build narratives in which they are blameless and lack the insight to see their share. Trials force us to form narratives, and real tawbah for big wrong stances is impossible without admitting fault. We lie to ourselves to avoid confrontation and shame, so the student must become an investigator of the truth. He reviews three dualities: reasons versus excuses for accountability, patterns versus mistakes for exposing one's real values, and states versus moments for being honest about whether life is a miserable baseline with brief joys. He returns to the self beneath all roles, the abd who puts on every hat and is the one resurrected, and to looking at life through milestones, ethics and circumstances. Being far from perfect should be encouraging, since it means room to grow. Finally he lays out muraqabah of actions, emotions and thoughts, and muhasabah modelled on raising a child: rewards and deprivations, answering a bad deed with a good one of the same kind, thorough tawbah with real changes, and one specific target at a time.

outline.heading: Opening
Reflect before you ask
outline.gist: Tazkiyah expects you to contemplate a question yourself until you hit a wall before handing it to a teacher.

outline.heading: The highest form of honesty
outline.gist: Honesty with people and with Allah are results of honesty with oneself.

outline.heading: Self-honesty among the four principles
outline.gist: Gradualism, building habits, abstaining from sin and self-honesty are the four principles of tazkiyah.

outline.heading: Narratives in disputes
outline.gist: In conflicts at work or with in-laws people tell airtight stories of their innocence and show no insight into their own part.

outline.heading: Trials force a narrative

outline.heading: Tawbah needs admitting fault
outline.gist: Repentance for major wrong stances and decisions requires the self-honesty to say 'I was wrong'.

outline.heading: Why we lie to ourselves
outline.gist: We avoid confronting ourselves out of shame, because the truth would demand change.

outline.heading: Be an investigator of the truth
outline.gist: Question your own claims like a detective; since argument with others goes nowhere, you need an inner regulating system.

outline.heading: Reasons versus excuses
outline.gist: An excuse ends accountability; a reason prompts you to keep asking why until you reach the root.

outline.heading: Patterns versus mistakes
outline.gist: Everyone makes mistakes, but a recurring one exposes a flawed belief that it is not a big deal.

outline.heading: No guarantee of forgiveness
outline.gist: We do not know which sins Allah will overlook, so part of us must stay alert and keep striving.

outline.heading: States versus moments
outline.gist: Life should be a state of contentment with moments of difficulty, not misery relieved by weekends and vacations.

outline.heading: The person beneath the different roles
outline.gist: Filmed with your child, friend and father you would seem three people; who is the one underneath?

outline.heading: The abd wears the hats
outline.gist: All roles die with you; define yourself as Allah's servant first, not a leader who then wears other hats.

outline.heading: Equal in essence whatever our roles
outline.gist: Allah gives some many roles and others few, but everyone is the same at the core; roles must not be mixed, like a professor parenting as a professor.

outline.heading: The Prophet's humility as an abd
outline.gist: He stayed humble even as leader because it was the servant wearing the hat.

outline.heading: Enjoying simply existing
outline.gist: Sit with the fact that you were created and loved, one unique outcome among countless possibilities.

outline.heading: Looking at life through lenses
outline.gist: Review your life through milestones, ethics, circumstances and roles to find patterns.

outline.heading: Steering by feedback
outline.gist: Self-honesty is a way of life, small responses to the terrain that keep you on the straight path.

outline.heading: Being far from perfect is good news
outline.gist: If you are at 40 percent you have huge room to grow; being told you are near your limit would be depressing.

outline.heading: Lies are paid back with interest
outline.gist: Honesty hurts first and eases later, while lies feel good now and are exposed even after death.

outline.heading: Muraqabah of actions, emotions and thoughts
outline.gist: Actions are easiest to observe, emotions harder, thoughts hardest.

outline.heading: Thoughts as a window into the heart
outline.gist: You are not accountable for a passing thought, but asking why it arose teaches you about yourself.

outline.heading: Start by observing one sin
outline.gist: Track one bad behaviour for a week or two to find patterns and reasons.

outline.heading: Muhasabah like raising a child
outline.gist: The ego needs balance of firmness and reward; align its desire for the carrot with what pleases Allah.

outline.heading: Answer a bad deed with a good one
outline.gist: If you speak badly of someone, do or say something good for that same person, which makes the sin costly.

outline.heading: Don't let a sin pass quickly
outline.gist: Like a child avoiding the conversation, the ego wants a quick tawbah; sit with the mistake until it becomes a deterrent.

outline.heading: Tawbah with a real plan
outline.gist: Repentance involves remorse rooted in correct belief and concrete changes to environment and lifestyle.

outline.heading: Choose one specific target
outline.gist: Muhasabah works on a precise behaviour, as parents who list ten faults at once change nothing.

outline.heading: Outro

uAkowMt2LEU.title: Lessons From 40 Years of Life
uAkowMt2LEU.one_line: On turning forty: the dua of Al-Ahqaf 46:15 for those at that age, then twelve life lessons for the young.
uAkowMt2LEU.summary: Khutbah marking his fortieth birthday. He begins with Al-Ahqaf 46:15, the dua Allah puts in the mouth of the person who reaches forty, the age at which the sum of a person's faculties peaks and at which most prophets received revelation. From it he draws five things for anyone at that age: ask for time to show gratitude for the blessings on you and your parents, to keep doing deeds that please Allah, and to see your children reformed; and establish two things now, repentance and belonging to the Muslims. The next verse promises acceptance of the best deeds and forgiveness of the worst for those who say it truthfully. Then, for the younger listeners, twelve written-down lessons: don't worry, be humble and stop comparing, face problems head-on, live beyond yourself because ignored suffering returns, be content with Allah but never with a corrupt status quo, stay focused on your mission, find your heart with Allah, be kind, dream ridiculously big, love your loved ones openly, admit when you are wrong, and invest in relationships. The emotional centre is Srebrenica: he was ten when the 1995 massacre shaped his understanding of the world and his commitment to the deen, and he tells the youth that nearly two years of Gaza must do the same for them.

outline.heading: Opening
Forty: when the sum of a person's faculties peaks
outline.gist: Al-Ahqaf 46:15 speaks of the one who reaches full strength and forty years. People peak physically earlier and socially later, but the scholars explain that the sum peaks at forty, the age Allah chose for most prophets, including Muhammad. The verse teaches three requests and two commitments.

outline.heading: Ask for time to be grateful for you and your parents
outline.gist: Ask Allah for more time, first so you can thank Him for the blessings on you and on your parents: reaching forty with faith still in your heart is a blessing on those who raised you too.

outline.heading: Deeds that please Him, and righteous children
outline.gist: Ask for time to keep doing deeds that please Allah, walking the path He chose for you, and for reform, good character and good deen in your children.

outline.heading: Repent now: tawbah needs no words
outline.gist: The first commitment to have established is repentance, now. It is the easiest thing of all: no words or moving lips, only inner remorse and the intention to be better and not return to old ways.

outline.heading: Belonging to the Muslims
outline.gist: The second commitment is to say 'I am among the Muslims' and truly feel part of this ummah and community. Whoever is past forty should go back to the verses and make the dua as taught.

outline.heading: The promise to those who say it truthfully
outline.gist: Al-Ahqaf 46:16: those who say it truthfully and live it have their best deeds accepted and their worst forgiven, among the people of Jannah. He then turns to twelve lessons for the young, written down because since forty he forgets.

outline.heading: Lesson one: don't worry too much
outline.gist: What is destined is destined, and worry has never changed an outcome; focus on what you can do. Worry punishes you twice, so cross the bridge when you reach it, trusting that with every difficulty comes enough ease to get through it.

outline.heading: Lesson two: be humble and stop comparing
outline.gist: Stop trying to prove your value; Allah knows you are valuable. People are not what you think and you are not what they think. Humility lets you learn and frees you from outdoing people living their own story.

outline.heading: Lesson three: don't run from your problems
outline.gist: Every problem you run from waits for you at the next destination. You are here to confront problems, and the longer you wait the harder they become.

outline.heading: Lesson four: live beyond yourself
outline.gist: If you ignore others' suffering, yours will one day be ignored. Live for haqq and justice, stand by the oppressed and refuse oppression, not just for this body and this experience.

outline.heading: Srebrenica: the massacre that shaped him
outline.gist: On July 11, thirty years after Srebrenica, he recalls being ten and watching the footage of 8,000 Muslims massacred within days. It scared him but gave him a cause: to be the voice of those treated as worthless, so their deaths are not in vain.

outline.heading: Gaza must shape the young
outline.gist: The young have watched nearly two years of bombardment of an area smaller than their own city, brutality few older people have seen. It must change how they see the world and what they commit to; ignore it and a day will come when you are ignored.

outline.heading: Lesson five: content with Allah, not with the status quo
outline.gist: Have ridha with what Allah has given you, but never with the corruption around you or the portion societies, governments and individuals choose to give you.

outline.heading: Ignore preachers who bless corruption
outline.gist: Be content with where you came from, how you look and how your life has gone, but if you accept a corrupt status quo you are part of the problem. A preacher who tells the poor to stay poor while thieves take everything is not teaching Islam.

outline.heading: Full rights first, then forgive if you wish
outline.gist: Accept whatever hand Allah deals you, but with people and society push back and refuse anything less than your full rights. Once you have them and are in a place of power, forgive or give them away if you want, but not before.

outline.heading: Lesson six: stay focused on your mission
outline.gist: Haters and supporters, those who join and those who leave, are variables that do not matter. Stay steadfast on what you are here to do and whom you serve; hold on to a like-minded companion if you have one, and keep moving as the Prophet did after losing many along the way.

outline.heading: Lesson seven: find your heart with Allah
outline.gist: Without finding the aspect of the deen, of His names, commands or gifts, that moves your heart, being Muslim is a heavy burden. Search the Quran, the Prophet's life and your own family and you will find it, and it becomes an endless supply of fuel.

outline.heading: Lesson eight: be kind
outline.gist: Life is too short to be anything else. If rahmah is not in your heart, hit the brakes; even in battle Muslims are commanded mercy. If you cannot be kind, hold your tongue and walk away until you can.

outline.heading: Lesson nine: dream ridiculously big
outline.gist: You get one arrow, so dream so big that even those who love you think you insane; reach for the stars and you reach the moon. Restricted dreams restrict how far you go.

outline.heading: Lesson ten: love your loved ones openly
outline.gist: A heart not filled with love for parents, siblings, spouse and friends is wasted. Love them with all your heart and show it, as the Prophet's heart was filled with love, once you have found your heart with Allah.

outline.heading: Lesson eleven: admit when you are wrong
outline.gist: Everyone is wrong at points; admitting it earns self-respect and others' respect and helps you grow. An ummah full of people who are all right cannot improve.

outline.heading: Lesson twelve: invest in your relationships
outline.gist: Relationships are the biggest investment of your life: the deeper and more meaningful they are, the better your quality of life and the more protected you are from everything that tries to change you.

outline.heading: Outro

stories.point: Forty is when the sum of a person's faculties peaks, which is why Allah chose it for prophecy and for this dua.

stories.who: Srebrenica, July 1995
stories.point: Watching the massacre of 8,000 Muslims at age ten scared him but gave him a cause: to be the voice of those treated that way.

stories.who: Preachers who tell the poor to stay poor
stories.point: False contentment that blesses corruption is not Islam; ridha is with Allah, not with thieves.

stories.who: The Prophet losing people along the way
stories.point: Many who started with him were not with him at the end; he stayed on mission, the easiest lesson to read from his life.

contemporary: Thirtieth anniversary of the Srebrenica genocide (July 11, 1995), 8,000 Muslims killed
Nearly two years of bombardment of Gaza, an area smaller than London, Ontario
Corrupt governments and thieves taking everything while preachers counsel the poor to accept it
His own fortieth birthday
takeaways: At or past forty, make the dua of 46:15: time for gratitude, continued good deeds and righteous children; repent now and belong to the ummah.
Stop worrying about what you cannot change and act on what you can; face problems early and head-on.
Let Gaza shape your worldview and commitments the way Srebrenica shaped his; never ignore suffering.
Accept Allah's decree but refuse corrupt status quos and demand full rights before you forgive.
Find the part of the deen that moves your heart and draw your fuel from it.
Be kind, love openly, admit mistakes and invest in relationships; dream ridiculously big.

30:29.ar: بَلِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ أَهۡوَآءَهُم بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمࣲۖ فَمَن يَهۡدِي مَنۡ أَضَلَّ ٱللَّهُۖ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
30:29.en: Nay, but those who do wrong follow their own lusts without knowledge. Who is able to guide him whom Allah hath sent astray? For such there are no helpers

30:30.ar: فَأَقِمۡ وَجۡهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفࣰ اۚ فِطۡرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيۡهَاۚ لَا تَبۡدِيلَ لِخَلۡقِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
30:30.en: So set thy purpose (O Muhammad) for religion as a man by nature upright - the nature (framed) of Allah, in which He hath created man. There is no altering (the laws of) Allah's creation. That is the right religion, but most men know not

30:31.ar: ۞مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيۡهِ وَٱتَّقُوهُ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَلَا تَكُونُواْ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
30:31.en: Turning unto Him (only); and be careful of your duty unto Him and establish worship, and be not of those who ascribe partners (unto Him)

30:32.ar: مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُواْ دِينَهُمۡ وَكَانُواْ شِيَعࣰ اۖ كُلُّ حِزۡبِۭ بِمَا لَدَيۡهِمۡ فَرِحُونَ
30:32.en: Of those who split up their religion and became schismatics, each sect exulting in its tenets

30:20.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنۡ خَلَقَكُم مِّن تُرَابࣲ ثُمَّ إِذَآ أَنتُم بَشَرࣱ تَنتَشِرُونَ
30:20.en: And of His signs is this: He created you of dust, and behold you human beings, ranging widely

30:21.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنۡ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا لِّتَسۡكُنُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيۡنَكُم مَّوَدَّةࣰ وَرَحۡمَةًۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
30:21.en: And of His signs is this: He created for you helpmeets from yourselves that ye might find rest in them, and He ordained between you love and mercy. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who reflect

30:22.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ خَلۡقُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱخۡتِلَٰفُ أَلۡسِنَتِكُمۡ وَأَلۡوَٰنِكُمۡۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّلۡعَٰلِمِينَ
30:22.en: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and colours. Lo! herein indeed are portents for men of knowledge

30:23.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ مَنَامُكُم بِٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ وَٱبۡتِغَآؤُكُم مِّن فَضۡلِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَسۡمَعُونَ
30:23.en: And of His signs is your slumber by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who heed

30:24.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ يُرِيكُمُ ٱلۡبَرۡقَ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعࣰ ا وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَيُحۡيِۦ بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَآۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
30:24.en: And of His signs is this: He showeth you the lightning for a fear and for a hope, and sendeth down water from the sky, and thereby quickeneth the earth after her death. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who understand

30:25.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَن تَقُومَ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِأَمۡرِهِۦۚ ثُمَّ إِذَا دَعَاكُمۡ دَعۡوَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِذَآ أَنتُمۡ تَخۡرُجُونَ
30:25.en: And of His signs is this: The heavens and the earth stand fast by His command, and afterward, when He calleth you, lo! from the earth ye will emerge

30:26.ar: وَلَهُۥ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ كُلࣱّ لَّهُۥ قَٰنِتُونَ
30:26.en: Unto Him belongeth whosoever is in the heavens and the earth. All are obedient unto Him

30:27.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَبۡدَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَلۡقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُۥ وَهُوَ أَهۡوَنُ عَلَيۡهِۚ وَلَهُ ٱلۡمَثَلُ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
30:27.en: He it is Who produceth creation, then reproduceth it, and it is easier for Him. His is the Sublime Similitude in the heavens and the earth. He is the Mighty, the Wise

30:28.ar: ضَرَبَ لَكُم مَّثَلࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَنفُسِكُمۡۖ هَل لَّكُم مِّن مَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُم مِّن شُرَكَآءَ فِي مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡ فَأَنتُمۡ فِيهِ سَوَآءࣱ تَخَافُونَهُمۡ كَخِيفَتِكُمۡ أَنفُسَكُمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
30:28.en: He coineth for you a similitude of yourselves. Have ye, from among those whom your right hands possess, partners in the wealth We have bestowed upon you, equal with you in respect thereof, so that ye fear them as ye fear each other (that ye ascribe unto Us partners out of that which We created)? Thus We display the revelations for people who have sense

45:23.ar: أَفَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمࣲ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِۦ وَقَلۡبِهِۦ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِۦ غِشَٰوَةࣰ فَمَن يَهۡدِيهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
45:23.en: Hast thou seen him who maketh his desire his god, and Allah sendeth him astray purposely, and sealeth up his hearing and his heart, and setteth on his sight a covering? Then who will lead him after Allah (hath condemned him)? Will ye not then heed

9:34.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡأَحۡبَارِ وَٱلرُّهۡبَانِ لَيَأۡكُلُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡنِزُونَ ٱلذَّهَبَ وَٱلۡفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَبَشِّرۡهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
9:34.en: O ye who believe! Lo! many of the (Jewish) rabbis and the (Christian) monks devour the wealth of mankind wantonly and debar (men) from the way of Allah. They who hoard up gold and silver and spend it not in the way of Allah, unto them give tidings (O Muhammad) of a painful doom

7:169.ar: فَخَلَفَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ خَلۡفࣱ وَرِثُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ يَأۡخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡأَدۡنَىٰ وَيَقُولُونَ سَيُغۡفَرُ لَنَا وَإِن يَأۡتِهِمۡ عَرَضࣱ مِّثۡلُهُۥ يَأۡخُذُوهُۚ أَلَمۡ يُؤۡخَذۡ عَلَيۡهِم مِّيثَٰقُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أَن لَّا يَقُولُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡحَقَّ وَدَرَسُواْ مَا فِيهِۗ وَٱلدَّارُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ خَيۡرࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
7:169.en: And a generation hath succeeded them who inherited the scriptures. They grasp the goods of this low life (as the price of evil-doing) and say: It will be forgiven us. And if there came to them (again) the offer of the like, they would accept it (and would sin again). Hath not the covenant of the Scripture been taken on their behalf that they should not speak aught concerning Allah save the truth? And they have studied that which is therein. And the abode of the Hereafter is better, for those who ward off (evil). Have ye then no sense

7:175.ar: وَٱتۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَبَأَ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا فَٱنسَلَخَ مِنۡهَا فَأَتۡبَعَهُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡغَاوِينَ
7:175.en: Recite unto them the tale of him to whom We gave Our revelations, but he sloughed them off, so Satan overtook him and he became of those who lead astray

7:176.ar: وَلَوۡ شِئۡنَا لَرَفَعۡنَٰهُ بِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّهُۥٓ أَخۡلَدَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُۚ فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡكَلۡبِ إِن تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡهِ يَلۡهَثۡ أَوۡ تَتۡرُكۡهُ يَلۡهَثۚ ذَّٰلِكَ مَثَلُ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَاۚ فَٱقۡصُصِ ٱلۡقَصَصَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
7:176.en: And had We willed We could have raised him by their means, but he clung to the earth and followed his own lust. Therefor his likeness is as the likeness of a dog: if thou attackest him he panteth with his tongue out, and if thou leavest him he panteth with his tongue out. Such is the likeness of the people who deny Our revelations. Narrate unto them the history (of the men of old), that haply they may take thought

3:67.ar: مَا كَانَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ يَهُودِيࣰّ ا وَلَا نَصۡرَانِيࣰّ ا وَلَٰكِن كَانَ حَنِيفࣰ ا مُّسۡلِمࣰ ا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
3:67.en: Abraham was not a Jew, nor yet a Christian; but he was an upright man who had surrendered (to Allah), and he was not of the idolaters

4:66.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّا كَتَبۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنِ ٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱخۡرُجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِكُم مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ فَعَلُواْ مَا يُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦ لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَشَدَّ تَثۡبِيتࣰ ا
4:66.en: And if We had decreed for them: Lay down your lives or go forth from your dwellings, but few of them would have done it; though if they did what they are exhorted to do it would be better for them, and more strengthening

4:67.ar: وَإِذࣰ ا لَّأٓتَيۡنَٰهُم مِّن لَّدُنَّآ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:67.en: And then We should bestow upon them from Our presence an immense reward

4:68.en: And should guide them unto a straight path

11:81.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓاْ إِلَيۡكَۖ فَأَسۡرِ بِأَهۡلِكَ بِقِطۡعࣲ مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَلَا يَلۡتَفِتۡ مِنكُمۡ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمۡرَأَتَكَۖ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ مَوۡعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبۡحُۚ أَلَيۡسَ ٱلصُّبۡحُ بِقَرِيبࣲ‏
11:81.en: (The messengers) said: O Lot! Lo! we are messengers of thy Lord; they shall not reach thee. So travel with thy people in a part of the night, and let not one of you turn round - (all) save thy wife. Lo! that which smiteth them will smite her (also). Lo! their tryst is (for) the morning. Is not the morning nigh

7:82.ar: وَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓاْ أَخۡرِجُوهُم مِّن قَرۡيَتِكُمۡۖ إِنَّهُمۡ أُنَاسࣱ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ
7:82.en: And the answer of his people was only that they said (one to another): Turn them out of your township. They are folk, forsooth, who keep pure

2:136.ar: قُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡنَا وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ وَٱلۡأَسۡبَاطِ وَمَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَمَآ أُوتِيَ ٱلنَّبِيُّونَ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيۡنَ أَحَدࣲ مِّنۡهُمۡ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ
2:136.en: Say (O Muslims): We believe in Allah and that which is revealed unto us and that which was revealed unto Abraham, and Ishmael, and Isaac, and Jacob, and the tribes, and that which Moses and Jesus received, and that which the prophets received from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and unto Him we have surrendered

2:137.ar: فَإِنۡ ءَامَنُواْ بِمِثۡلِ مَآ ءَامَنتُم بِهِۦ فَقَدِ ٱهۡتَدَواْۖ وَّإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَإِنَّمَا هُمۡ فِي شِقَاقࣲۖ فَسَيَكۡفِيكَهُمُ ٱللَّهُۚ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
2:137.en: And if they believe in the like of that which ye believe, then are they rightly guided. But if they turn away, then are they in schism, and Allah will suffice thee (for defence) against them. He is the Hearer, the Knower

2:138.ar: صِبۡغَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَنۡ أَحۡسَنُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ صِبۡغَةࣰۖ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ عَٰبِدُونَ
2:138.en: (We take our) colour from Allah, and who is better than Allah at colouring. We are His worshippers

6:159.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُواْ دِينَهُمۡ وَكَانُواْ شِيَعࣰ ا لَّسۡتَ مِنۡهُمۡ فِي شَيۡءٍۚ إِنَّمَآ أَمۡرُهُمۡ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
6:159.en: Lo! As for those who sunder their religion and become schismatics, no concern at all hast thou with them. Their case will go to Allah, Who then will tell them what they used to do

6:160.ar: مَن جَآءَ بِٱلۡحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُۥ عَشۡرُ أَمۡثَالِهَاۖ وَمَن جَآءَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ فَلَا يُجۡزَىٰٓ إِلَّا مِثۡلَهَا وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
6:160.en: Whoso bringeth a good deed will receive tenfold the like thereof, while whoso bringeth an ill-deed will be awarded but the like thereof; and they will not be wronged

6:161.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّنِي هَدَىٰنِي رَبِّيٓ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ دِينࣰ ا قِيَمࣰ ا مِّلَّةَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ حَنِيفࣰ اۚ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
6:161.en: Say: Lo! As for me, my Lord hath guided me unto a straight path, a right religion, the community of Abraham, the upright, who was no idolater

OpkqJZIykBU.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Ar-Rum (30:29-32)
OpkqJZIykBU.one_line: Desire, not reason, breeds shirk; set your face to the religion of fitrah, which works with human nature, and do not split it into sects.
OpkqJZIykBU.summary: No rational person really believes Allah has partners; people get there by following desire, which the Quran condemns, while it always praises those who reason. Three centuries of tyranny and deliberate ignorance shrank both minds and hearts, so the ummah now distrusts thinking and expects quick revival; rebuilding takes long investment in people, not buildings, as the Prophet showed. Verse 30 commands setting one's whole self to the religion, inclining away from shirk and desire, because Islam is the religion of fitrah: every command fits human nature, rational, material, social and moral, as Ibn Ashur explains. Parents and surroundings corrupt the child born on fitrah; political tyranny corrupts whole peoples, and once fitrah is lost values invert, as with the people of Lot. The four commands are: set your face to the religion while turning back to Allah whenever you slip, be mindful of Him, establish prayer, and do not be among those who split their religion into factions, each pleased with itself. He closes by explaining bid'ah through its only two Quranic uses and the hadith of the man standing in the sun and the companions who vowed never to marry: innovation means adding to religion what harms human nature.

outline.heading: Ar-Rum and three kinds of law
outline.gist: Divine laws are natural, human and beneficial; whoever works with them succeeds and whoever defies them fails.

outline.heading: Recap: six signs and the parable of partners
outline.gist: Five laws we live and one we see on the Last Day, followed by the parable of servants as partners.

outline.heading: Following desire lies behind every sin
outline.gist: No sane person truly believes in partners; following desire spoils life, and the clever one holds himself to account.

outline.heading: Logic was never the enemy of the sacred sciences
outline.gist: The surah's conclusions are reached by reason; logic was among the first subjects students learned, and the Quran cannot be understood without it.

outline.heading: The Quran blames desire, never reason
outline.gist: It praises those who reflect and understand; even scholars fall only when they follow desire, like the one who clung to the earth.

outline.heading: Three hundred years of tyranny and ignorance
outline.gist: Foreign and local rulers deliberately kept the ummah ignorant, turning a literate and upright people into one where bribery and interest are easy.

outline.heading: Destruction is quick, building is slow
outline.gist: We expect instant revival after centuries in a dark room; scholarly output of the last three centuries cannot compare with earlier eras.

outline.heading: Mind and heart must grow together
outline.gist: Decline made us suspicious of thought; a big mind with a small heart lacks tazkiyah, and a big heart with a small mind is a naive dervish.

outline.heading: Invest in people, not walls
outline.gist: Opening a school needs forty qualified teachers; the Prophet had no carpets or roof but built a nation by investing in people.

outline.heading: Verses 30-32 recited: the open ta of 'fitrat'
outline.gist: Beware of making the ta heavy after the emphatic letters; it is written open here.

outline.heading: 'Aqim': establishing a thing with its structure
outline.gist: The fa follows from the signs and parable; the root q-w-m means doing something with all its conditions, as with marriage or a partnership.

outline.heading: Your face means your whole self
outline.gist: 'Face' stands for the self, as in 'the face has succeeded' said to Abdullah ibn Unays; a hanif is one who turns away from error.

outline.heading: Hanif: turning from shirk and worldly gain
outline.gist: The early generation's motto was being hanif; one can wear the turban and serve religion for gain without being hanif.

outline.heading: Fitrah is far more than sexual instinct
outline.gist: Ibn Ashur lists rational, material, social and moral fitrah; Islam's every command fits human nature.

outline.heading: Muslims were realists, not mystifiers
outline.gist: Muslims looked for causes rather than miracles; fitrah includes cleanliness and regulated relations between the sexes, since no one is happier living in zina.

outline.heading: Zakat and honouring parents are fitrah
outline.gist: Giving surplus to the needy and caring for parents are natural; pushing children out at eighteen goes against fitrah.

outline.heading: Allah never commanded against fitrah
outline.gist: He could have commanded hard things, but only asks what benefits us; doing what we are exhorted to brings firmness and guidance.

outline.heading: Every child is born on fitrah
outline.gist: Parents make the child Jewish, Christian or Magian, as people mutilate a healthy newborn animal; children learn filth and rudeness from their surroundings.

outline.heading: The child who shouts at his parents
outline.gist: A Sudanese sheikh sent a girl to fetch her mother, then sent the mother to fetch hers, to find the root of the problem.

outline.heading: Islam protects the young person's drive
outline.gist: Fitrah fills youth with a will to achieve; corrupted, it can turn cruel, and political tyranny does exactly this.

outline.heading: When fitrah is lost values invert
outline.gist: Lot's people mocked purity itself and could not be reformed; then the seeker of what is lawful becomes the outcast.

outline.heading: The upright religion and natural modesty
outline.gist: Religion is valuable when it guards your fitrah, such as natural modesty that early exposure to the forbidden destroys; most people think religion forbids enjoyment.

outline.heading: All prophets came to strengthen fitrah
outline.gist: Drugs and zina promise pleasure but end in ruin; Al-Baqarah's 'colouring of Allah' shows all prophets brought the same nature-affirming message.

outline.heading: Turning back to Him and being mindful
outline.gist: Whenever you drift from fitrah, return by repentance, and guard yourself from His punishment.

outline.heading: Establish prayer and do not split the religion
outline.gist: Prayer too must be 'established' with all its parts; those who split their religion turned a simple, natural faith into factions.

outline.heading: Factions and the parallel in Al-An'am
outline.gist: Shi'ah means a group bound by a tie; Al-An'am's closing verses carry the same words, and our da'wah is to bring people back to their nature.

outline.heading: Each faction pleased with itself
outline.gist: Blameworthy joy is the joy of self-delusion; to know Islam is true, check its rulings against your fitrah.

outline.heading: Marriage and the ban on seclusion honour fitrah
outline.gist: Public marriage gives dignity to intimacy; forbidding seclusion and approaching zina reflects knowledge of what we cannot resist.

outline.heading: The four commands, and religions that harm the self
outline.gist: Self-flagellation, endless mourning and enforced celibacy are not from any true religion.

outline.heading: The man in the sun and the man who refused marriage
outline.gist: The Prophet told Abu Isra'il to sit in the shade and finish his fast, and told those who renounced marriage that he marries.

outline.heading: Bid'ah protects fitrah
outline.gist: Innovation is a much misused word; it exists to guard the religion from what corrupts nature.

outline.heading: Bid'ah in the Quran: two places only
outline.gist: 'I am no novelty among the messengers' and the monasticism they invented: innovation means adding what harms human nature.

outline.heading: Outro

Yqg2tPCxYQ0.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Honesty, Episode 7
Yqg2tPCxYQ0.one_line: Self-honesty as the root of all honesty, its link to self-value, and the exercise of stripping away every role to find the servant beneath.
Yqg2tPCxYQ0.summary: The sheikh opens by explaining why tazkiyah is a delicate discipline: knowledge that is not practised becomes a weapon the ego uses against its owner, as in the hadith of the scholar, martyr and philanthropist thrown first into the Fire. He then argues that honesty matters most inwardly. There are exemptions for what we say to others, but none for lying to oneself, and lying to people is only a symptom of an inner habit. He connects this to self-value: if worth is derived from one's own flattering opinion, honest self-assessment feels threatening, so people avoid feedback and stay stagnant. He recounts asking friends how they saw him and being devastated by one answer. The central reflection is to remove every role (parent, spouse, job) and ask who remains: a servant of Allah, which is the identity one meets on the Day of Judgment. Khalid ibn al-Walid serving after his demotion and the emigrants leaving status behind illustrate it, while Pharaoh shows how far self-deception can go. Even without change, self-honesty brings humility before Allah. He introduces muraqabah and muhasabah and assigns two tasks: the roles reflection and seeking honest feedback from people who love you.

outline.heading: Teaching tazkiyah in a new context
outline.gist: How the programme began and why teaching it here, to brothers and sisters, has differed from how he learned it in Syria.

outline.heading: Knowledge without tazkiyah backfires
outline.gist: Unpractised knowledge lets the ego justify wrongdoing; the hadith of the scholar, martyr and philanthropist first into the Fire shows tazkiyah is the shield.

outline.heading: Why begin with self-honesty
outline.gist: This iteration of the course starts with self-honesty as the foundation.

outline.heading: Only attend if you will practise
outline.gist: Tazkiyah taken as theory harms you; it demands trying, failing and persevering.

outline.heading: Interlude
Learning to answer your own questions
outline.gist: His role is to give a method for working through the soul's struggles, since no teacher can answer every question.

outline.heading: Interlude
No exemption for lying to yourself
outline.gist: Honesty with people has exceptions, but honesty with oneself has none, because it underlies honesty with Allah.

outline.heading: Inner lies produce outer lies
outline.gist: Whatever we do internally shows externally; lying to others grows from a long habit of lying to oneself.

outline.heading: People lie for gain or fear
outline.gist: Once you stop caring how people see you, lying to them loses its point; outer lying is a symptom, not the disease.

outline.heading: Self-value is a divine constant
outline.gist: Worth as a human is granted by Allah and does not rise or fall; only value within a team or role varies.

outline.heading: Deriving value from self-opinion blocks honesty
outline.gist: If your worth rests on how you view yourself, you will lie to protect that view, as with believing you are good at a game.

outline.heading: You cannot fix what you will not see
outline.gist: Honest self-assessment is what makes improvement possible, as spouse, parent, friend or colleague.

outline.heading: His own experience of asking friends
outline.gist: Asked to survey his friends at 26, he was brought to tears by how one friend actually saw him.

outline.heading: Seek feedback from people who love you
outline.gist: Ask friends what they truly think; being offended shows you have not yet valued self-honesty.

outline.heading: Feedback as a gift of your flaws
outline.gist: Someone who points out your faults gives you what you could not obtain alone; recap of the tools of looking inward.

outline.heading: Self-honesty as a shield against praise and criticism
outline.gist: There is always some truth in what people say, but someone who knows himself is neither crushed by insult nor inflated by praise.

outline.heading: Removing every role: who is left?
outline.gist: Imagine losing every role you hold and ask who remains.

outline.heading: Khalifah and abd
outline.gist: Allah describes us as stewards who carry roles, as Dawud carried many, and as servants beneath all roles.

outline.heading: The raw self is a servant of Allah
outline.gist: Beneath the layers is a creation loved by Allah; knowing this brings a lasting state of peace rather than passing moments.

outline.heading: When people become their hat
outline.gist: Celebrities who collapse after retirement had no self beneath the role; know who you are before you meet yourself on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Khalid ibn al-Walid serving after demotion
outline.gist: Demoted by Umar, Khalid kept serving wherever he was placed, because he knew who he was beneath any position.

outline.heading: The emigrants left their status behind
outline.gist: The Meccan emigrants lost wealth, tribe and reputation in Madinah and endured because they did not define themselves by roles.

outline.heading: Pharaoh believed his own claim
outline.gist: He argues Pharaoh likely believed he was lord most high, having let applause define him until self-deception was complete.

outline.heading: A part of you always knows
outline.gist: The conscience always registers self-deception; the work is to amplify that voice instead of drowning it.

outline.heading: Rewriting the story after a dispute
outline.gist: After a marital argument we build a version that blames the other, as children lie until they think they can be proven wrong.

outline.heading: Allah is the camera within
outline.gist: We lie about thoughts and feelings because no one can prove them, but Allah records what happens inside.

outline.heading: Self-honesty brings humility even without change
outline.gist: Knowing your faults lets you approach Allah as one at fault; the forgiven in the sunnah never argued their case.

outline.heading: Introducing muraqabah and muhasabah
outline.gist: Self-observation and self-accountability are the tools that turn honesty into change.

outline.heading: Observing one flaw
outline.gist: Pick one flaw you were not honest about, such as losing your temper or a recurring sin, and track when and why it happens.

outline.heading: Accountability through reward and deprivation
outline.gist: An early scholar taught raising the demand whenever the ego objects; like parenting, threats you do not carry out teach nothing.

outline.heading: Task one: exist without your roles
outline.gist: Spend time reflecting on yourself stripped of every role; it is emotional and he will revisit it weekly.

outline.heading: Task two: ask for honest feedback
outline.gist: Ask people who love you how you are to them, and reflect on why it bothers you or why it does not.

outline.heading: What saddened him most
outline.gist: Not the criticism itself but how long he had been oblivious to his effect on a friend.

outline.heading: The Prophet's culture of direct feedback
outline.gist: The Prophet gave and received honest feedback without breaking relationships; our culture has replaced it with the feedback sandwich.

outline.heading: Outro

30:24.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ يُرِيكُمُ ٱلۡبَرۡقَ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعࣰ ا وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَيُحۡيِۦ بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَآۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
30:24.en: And of His signs is this: He showeth you the lightning for a fear and for a hope, and sendeth down water from the sky, and thereby quickeneth the earth after her death. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who understand

30:25.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَن تَقُومَ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِأَمۡرِهِۦۚ ثُمَّ إِذَا دَعَاكُمۡ دَعۡوَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِذَآ أَنتُمۡ تَخۡرُجُونَ
30:25.en: And of His signs is this: The heavens and the earth stand fast by His command, and afterward, when He calleth you, lo! from the earth ye will emerge

30:26.ar: وَلَهُۥ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ كُلࣱّ لَّهُۥ قَٰنِتُونَ
30:26.en: Unto Him belongeth whosoever is in the heavens and the earth. All are obedient unto Him

30:27.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَبۡدَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَلۡقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُۥ وَهُوَ أَهۡوَنُ عَلَيۡهِۚ وَلَهُ ٱلۡمَثَلُ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
30:27.en: He it is Who produceth creation, then reproduceth it, and it is easier for Him. His is the Sublime Similitude in the heavens and the earth. He is the Mighty, the Wise

30:28.ar: ضَرَبَ لَكُم مَّثَلࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَنفُسِكُمۡۖ هَل لَّكُم مِّن مَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُم مِّن شُرَكَآءَ فِي مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡ فَأَنتُمۡ فِيهِ سَوَآءࣱ تَخَافُونَهُمۡ كَخِيفَتِكُمۡ أَنفُسَكُمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
30:28.en: He coineth for you a similitude of yourselves. Have ye, from among those whom your right hands possess, partners in the wealth We have bestowed upon you, equal with you in respect thereof, so that ye fear them as ye fear each other (that ye ascribe unto Us partners out of that which We created)? Thus We display the revelations for people who have sense

30:29.ar: بَلِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ أَهۡوَآءَهُم بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمࣲۖ فَمَن يَهۡدِي مَنۡ أَضَلَّ ٱللَّهُۖ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
30:29.en: Nay, but those who do wrong follow their own lusts without knowledge. Who is able to guide him whom Allah hath sent astray? For such there are no helpers

30:30.ar: فَأَقِمۡ وَجۡهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفࣰ اۚ فِطۡرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيۡهَاۚ لَا تَبۡدِيلَ لِخَلۡقِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
30:30.en: So set thy purpose (O Muhammad) for religion as a man by nature upright - the nature (framed) of Allah, in which He hath created man. There is no altering (the laws of) Allah's creation. That is the right religion, but most men know not

8:5.ar: كَمَآ أَخۡرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَيۡتِكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِنَّ فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ لَكَٰرِهُونَ
8:5.en: Even as thy Lord caused thee (Muhammad) to go forth from thy home with the Truth, and lo! a party of the believers were averse (to it)

8:6.ar: يُجَٰدِلُونَكَ فِي ٱلۡحَقِّ بَعۡدَ مَا تَبَيَّنَ كَأَنَّمَا يُسَاقُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَوۡتِ وَهُمۡ يَنظُرُونَ
8:6.en: Disputing with thee of the Truth after it had been made manifest, as if they were being driven to death visible

4:77.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهُمۡ كُفُّوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَكُمۡ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ إِذَا فَرِيقࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ يَخۡشَوۡنَ ٱلنَّاسَ كَخَشۡيَةِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡ أَشَدَّ خَشۡيَةࣰۚ وَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَا لِمَ كَتَبۡتَ عَلَيۡنَا ٱلۡقِتَالَ لَوۡلَآ أَخَّرۡتَنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ قَرِيبࣲۗ قُلۡ مَتَٰعُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا قَلِيلࣱ وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ خَيۡرࣱ لِّمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ وَلَا تُظۡلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا
4:77.en: Hast thou not seen those unto whom it was said: Withhold your hands, establish worship and pay the poordue, but when fighting was prescribed for them behold! a party of them fear mankind even as their fear of Allah or with greater fear, and say: Our Lord! Why hast Thou ordained fighting for us? If only Thou wouldst give us respite yet a while! Say (unto them, O Muhammad): The comfort of this world is scant; the Hereafter will be better for him who wardeth off (evil); and ye will not be wronged the down upon a date-stone

4:78.ar: أَيۡنَمَا تَكُونُواْ يُدۡرِككُّمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ وَلَوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِي بُرُوجࣲ مُّشَيَّدَةࣲۗ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ حَسَنَةࣱ يَقُولُواْ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةࣱ يَقُولُواْ هَٰذِهِۦ مِنۡ عِندِكَۚ قُلۡ كُلࣱّ مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَالِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ لَا يَكَادُونَ يَفۡقَهُونَ حَدِيثࣰ ا
4:78.en: Wheresoever ye may be, death will overtake you, even though ye were in lofty towers. Yet if a happy thing befalleth them they say: This is from Allah; and if an evil thing befalleth them they say: This is of thy doing (O Muhammad). Say (unto them): All is from Allah. What is amiss with these people that they come not nigh to understand a happening

39:3.ar: أَلَا لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡخَالِصُۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَ مَا نَعۡبُدُهُمۡ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ زُلۡفَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحۡكُمُ بَيۡنَهُمۡ فِي مَا هُمۡ فِيهِ يَخۡتَلِفُونَۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي مَنۡ هُوَ كَٰذِبࣱ كَفَّارࣱ‏
39:3.en: Surely pure religion is for Allah only. And those who choose protecting friends beside Him (say): We worship them only that they may bring us near unto Allah. Lo! Allah will judge between them concerning that wherein they differ. Lo! Allah guideth not him who is a liar, an ingrate

54:7.ar: خُشَّعًا أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمۡ جَرَادࣱ مُّنتَشِرࣱ‏
54:7.en: With downcast eyes, they come forth from the graves as they were locusts spread abroad

6:94.ar: وَلَقَدۡ جِئۡتُمُونَا فُرَٰدَىٰ كَمَا خَلَقۡنَٰكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲ وَتَرَكۡتُم مَّا خَوَّلۡنَٰكُمۡ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِكُمۡۖ وَمَا نَرَىٰ مَعَكُمۡ شُفَعَآءَكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمۡتُمۡ أَنَّهُمۡ فِيكُمۡ شُرَكَٰٓؤُاْۚ لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَضَلَّ عَنكُم مَّا كُنتُمۡ تَزۡعُمُونَ
6:94.en: Now have ye come unto Us solitary as We did create you at the first, and ye have left behind you all that We bestowed upon you, and We behold not with you those your intercessors, of whom ye claimed that they possessed a share in you. Now is the bond between you severed, and that which ye presumed hath failed you

6:100.ar: وَجَعَلُواْ لِلَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ ٱلۡجِنَّ وَخَلَقَهُمۡۖ وَخَرَقُواْ لَهُۥ بَنِينَ وَبَنَٰتِۭ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمࣲۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
6:100.en: Yet they ascribe as partners unto Him the jinn, although He did create them, and impute falsely, without knowledge, sons and daughters unto Him. Glorified be He and High Exalted above (all) that they ascribe (unto Him)

6:101.ar: بَدِيعُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لَهُۥ وَلَدࣱ وَلَمۡ تَكُن لَّهُۥ صَٰحِبَةࣱۖ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
6:101.en: The Originator of the heavens and the earth! How can He have a child, when there is for Him no consort, when He created all things and is Aware of all things

16:57.ar: وَيَجۡعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡبَنَٰتِ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَلَهُم مَّا يَشۡتَهُونَ
16:57.en: And they assign unto Allah daughters - Be He Glorified! - and unto themselves what they desire

45:23.ar: أَفَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمࣲ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِۦ وَقَلۡبِهِۦ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِۦ غِشَٰوَةࣰ فَمَن يَهۡدِيهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
45:23.en: Hast thou seen him who maketh his desire his god, and Allah sendeth him astray purposely, and sealeth up his hearing and his heart, and setteth on his sight a covering? Then who will lead him after Allah (hath condemned him)? Will ye not then heed

MmK9XqZykh0.speaker_note: continues his weekly Arabic tafsir of Ar-Rum, refers to growing up in a Syrian village and fifteen years with youth here
MmK9XqZykh0.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Ar-Rum (30:24-29)
MmK9XqZykh0.one_line: Allah's laws are His: no good without its price, the laws undone on the Last Day, and the parable of slaves as partners exposing shirk as desire.
MmK9XqZykh0.summary: Natural cause and effect, such as effort bringing provision, are Allah's own laws, not Western ones; claiming reliance on Allah while ignoring them is not tawakkul, and praying for victory without building a nation is like a bachelor praying for a son. The early Arabs, hardened by the desert, were realistic enough for the Quran, while ignorance in later centuries bred fantasy and superstition. Even the law against seclusion with the opposite sex reflects Allah's knowledge of our nature. Verse 24 teaches that lightning brings both fear and hope: no good comes without hardship, so young people who want the goal of a footballer or a rich man must accept the years of effort behind it; only Paradise exceeds what we paid. Verses 25-27 describe a sixth law, seen only on the Last Day, when Allah orders heaven and earth to undo every law and calls the dead from the earth; repeating creation is easier by our own measure, yet His is the highest example. The parable of verses 28-29 asks whether we make our servants equal partners in our wealth; no one does, so how could Allah share His dominion? People invent partners not from conviction but from desire, wanting someone to bend the rules for them, while tawhid closes that door.

outline.heading: Ar-Rum and our relationship with Allah's laws
outline.gist: Each surah from Al-Qasas to As-Sajdah treats one human relationship; this one, with divine laws, is among the least understood.

outline.heading: Natural laws are Allah's laws
outline.gist: Gravity, effort and reward, skill and income, health and care are His laws, not Western ones, and deserve reverence.

outline.heading: Laws are not above Allah's will
outline.gist: He taught that provision is from Him and that He can override His laws, but defying them is not respect for Him.

outline.heading: Idleness is not tawakkul
outline.gist: Sitting at home claiming reliance on Allah defies His law; no family, and no Lord, honours that.

outline.heading: Nations rise by justice, knowledge and order
outline.gist: A corrupt, divided nation will not rise however much it prays; seeing reality is painful but necessary to change it.

outline.heading: Like a bachelor praying for a son
outline.gist: A village sheikh compared praying for victory without effort to a bachelor begging Allah for a child instead of marrying.

outline.heading: Ignorance breeds fantasy and superstition
outline.gist: Ignorant societies inflate jinn and magic and build hopes on things unconnected to reality.

outline.heading: The Arabs were a realistic people
outline.gist: Desert life made them face hard truths, so they could learn Allah's laws and the Prophet could raise them.

outline.heading: The believers who disliked fighting
outline.gist: When comfort set in at Madinah some disliked going out; no nation rises without people ready to sacrifice.

outline.heading: Volunteer armies and the Prophet's sweat
outline.gist: Early Muslim fighters refused pay; every step the Prophet took cost him effort and blood, so we cannot expect less.

outline.heading: Seclusion with the opposite sex as a law of nature
outline.gist: The prohibition reflects Allah's knowledge that humans cannot resist over time, whatever their piety.

outline.heading: Verse 24 recited: lightning, fear and hope
outline.gist: The fifth law describes life as a cycle that ends and begins again.

outline.heading: No good comes without fear
outline.gist: Lightning frightens but promises rain; what comes cheaply leaves cheaply.

outline.heading: 'Were it not for hardship all would be masters'
outline.gist: Al-Mutanabbi's line shows leadership costs generosity and courage; young people here often want only the easiest path.

outline.heading: Flee the lightning and you lose the rain
outline.gist: High ambition needs courage and endurance; whoever refuses the fear refuses the reward.

outline.heading: Reviving dead land, at a price
outline.gist: Life returns to dead earth, but always with effort and cost.

outline.heading: The footballer's goal and the quick fortune
outline.gist: Youth see the trophy, not the years of pre-dawn training; they chase fast money without knowing the rich slept in their cars.

outline.heading: Achievements feel ordinary once paid for, except Paradise
outline.gist: The dream of being a doctor fades once you pay its full price; only Allah's reward exceeds what you gave.

outline.heading: Verses 25-27 recited
outline.gist: Heaven and earth stand by His command, then He calls you from the earth.

outline.heading: Review of the five laws
outline.gist: Dust, the need for a spouse, diversity, the balance of sleep and work, and no good without its price; despising a people means despising Allah's work.

outline.heading: Sixth law: heaven and earth undone by His command
outline.gist: On the Last Day the sky splits, mountains become wool and the sun is folded: every law is broken.

outline.heading: One call brings everyone out of the earth
outline.gist: The first five laws we live daily; this one we will know only on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: All are devoutly obedient to Him
outline.gist: Qunut is standing in humble reverence, as we should in prayer; every creature and every law obeys Him.

outline.heading: Coming to Him alone and uncovered
outline.gist: Wealth, titles and clothes are left behind; only deeds cover a person on that Day.

outline.heading: Repeating creation is easier by our measure
outline.gist: Doing a thing twice is easier than once, so why doubt resurrection? Claiming life arose by chance defies the simplest law of cause.

outline.heading: His is the highest example; the Mighty, the Wise
outline.gist: The comparison only brings the idea near; every law holds a wisdom, known or not.

outline.heading: Verses 28-29 recited: a parable from yourselves
outline.gist: A new passage on partners and desire.

outline.heading: Parables because we cannot grasp His essence
outline.gist: We know how our eyes and ears work but not how Allah sees or hears; whoever speaks of that speaks without knowledge.

outline.heading: Living by 'no one owns but Allah'
outline.gist: Whoever truly believes none owns, provides or acts but Allah lives with courage and never sells his principles.

outline.heading: Would you make your servants equal partners?
outline.gist: No one gives a servant equal share, status and awe; partnership requires equality, which is why jurists disfavoured partnership between father and son.

outline.heading: Giving Allah what you refuse for yourselves
outline.gist: The idolaters admitted Allah created all yet gave Him partners and daughters they would not accept for themselves.

outline.heading: 'Bal': shirk comes from desire, not conviction
outline.gist: No sane person truly believes Allah has partners; those who wronged themselves followed desire, which blinds.

outline.heading: Why people want partners: someone to bend the rules
outline.gist: People hate the honest minister who refuses favours; idols and intermediaries let them make the unlawful lawful, and tawhid stops that.

outline.heading: Follow desire or follow the truth
outline.gist: Whoever takes desire as a god is left astray with no helper.

themes.label: Allah's laws (sunan) in creation and society
themes.note: Natural cause and effect are Allah's laws; ignoring them while praying for results misunderstands both faith and life.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Reliance on Allah never means abandoning the means He set.

UayrFsdqCcc.speaker: adnan
UayrFsdqCcc.speaker_note: First-person launch of his own 'Achieving the Outcomes' series ('the series that I'm going to start for the next 10 or 11 weeks'); refers to his earlier khutbah series on the second pledge of Aqabah and to teaching children at this masjid; title names no other speaker.
UayrFsdqCcc.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Defining the Metrics
UayrFsdqCcc.one_line: Series opener: success as a Muslim must be measured by the Prophet's metrics, transformed ethics and conduct, not by culturally driven ritual checklists.
UayrFsdqCcc.summary: Opening khutbah of the 'Achieving the Outcomes' series. Islam was always destined to be lived on earth, so Muslims must be clear about what it is meant to achieve here, not only in the Hereafter. Against two years of Gaza he insists listeners never grow desensitized, and that the ground can be recovered in record time if the Prophet's footsteps are followed, as he transformed Arabia in 23 years. The first question is metrics. If people had abandoned idols but kept lying, cheating, murdering and oppressing, what would have been achieved? And who defines a good person; he mocks those who certify themselves. His test case is the migration to Abyssinia, which he says puzzled him for years: Islam's character could not be assessed in Mecca while Muslims were oppressed, since the oppressed often become worse oppressors once freed, so Abyssinia was the first true test. Ja'far, aged 21, presented Islam to the Negus purely as a before-and-after of ethics, honesty, trust, kinship and protecting orphans, with no mention of rituals, because rituals were the vehicle and conduct the outcome. The first pledge of Aqabah likewise asked for no theft, adultery, murder or false testimony, and the second pledge's demands existed to protect those outcomes. Today alcohol is clearly haram while cheating is tolerated; the fix is to raise the neglected standards, not lower the kept ones. He closes by saying children cannot be convinced of Islam without living examples at home, and that knowing the metrics produces a useful humility.

outline.heading: Opening
What is Islam meant to achieve?
outline.gist: He opens with the verses usually heard at the end of a khutbah and launches a ten- or eleven-week series on outcomes: what being Muslim should produce personally, communally, for the ummah and for humanity, in this world as well as the next.

outline.heading: Destined for earth from day one
outline.gist: Long before Adam knew himself, Allah declared He would place a steward on earth, so the way of life the Prophet embodied was always meant to be lived here. Do Muslims have clarity on its outcomes?

outline.heading: Two years of Gaza: never grow desensitized
outline.gist: He prays for relief, protection of the innocent and riddance of every oppressor, homegrown or foreign. After nearly two years of rubble, starving children and body parts on screens, he begs listeners never to scroll past it unmoved.

outline.heading: Lost ground can be regained in record time
outline.gist: Nothing changes until Muslims sort themselves out, and the road is long. With commitment, sound intentions and the devotion of the young it can be made up quickly; the Prophet changed Arabia in 23 years, and following him obligates hope.

outline.heading: If they broke the idols but kept lying and stealing
outline.gist: Hypothetically, if people abandoned shirk but went on lying, stealing, murdering, cheating in business, corrupt in politics and racist, what would have been achieved? True tawhid would not allow it, but the question stands.

outline.heading: Who gets to define a good person?
outline.gist: He mocks people who certify themselves as good, a definition he thought belonged to God. Asking who defines goodness is central to understanding what the Prophet offered.

outline.heading: Why did they go to Abyssinia?
outline.gist: For years he could not see why about a hundred companions crossed the Red Sea to a different culture, religion and language and mostly stayed fifteen years, with a few such as Uthman and his wife returning early.

outline.heading: You cannot judge the character of the oppressed
outline.gist: In Makkah Islam's character could not be assessed: the oppressed are bound together by weakness, and history shows many become worse oppressors once freed. Abyssinia was the first real test, and they returned about nine hundred strong.

outline.heading: Quraysh send Amr to bring them back
outline.gist: Losing a hundred of its people to Abyssinia was a political humiliation, so Amr ibn al-As, who knew the king well, came with gifts and bribes, calling the refugees runaway children with weeping parents.

outline.heading: A just king hears them out
outline.gist: The Negus had no reason to care about a hundred Arabs but chose to hear them. They chose 21-year-old Ja'far, a fine speaker who organised his points and simply presented Islam as he had lived it.

outline.heading: Ja'far: who we were in jahiliyyah
outline.gist: We worshipped rocks, which mattered to a Christian king, ate carrion, were bad neighbours, severed kinship and let the strong devour the weak, with no law and little compassion.

outline.heading: Ja'far: what the Prophet commanded
outline.gist: A man whose lineage and integrity we knew commanded us to worship Allah alone, speak truthfully, keep trusts, be good neighbours and relatives, and forbade oppression, consuming orphans' wealth and false testimony.

outline.heading: Rituals are the vehicle, conduct the outcome
outline.gist: Ja'far never went into rituals, because they were the means, not the outcome. The before-and-after of their conduct was enough for the Negus to let them stay.

outline.heading: The first test of Islamic character
outline.gist: Ja'far was no philosopher in his fifties; at 21 he could say he now thought differently about family, ethics, integrity, community and life itself.

outline.heading: What do you have to show for being Muslim?
outline.gist: After a lifetime as a Muslim, what can you present? If it is not what the Prophet and the companions showed, we are in trouble, and we are, because we define success in a culturally driven way, caught in superficial details instead of essence.

outline.heading: The six terms of the first pledge
outline.gist: Before the second pledge of Aqabah came the first, on the terms at the end of Al-Mumtahanah: no shirk, theft, adultery or killing, literal or through the abuse that kills a soul, and readiness to answer any call with time and wealth.

outline.heading: The second pledge protected the first
outline.gist: The last term forbids false testimony and corruption. These were the outcomes; the articles of the second pledge, covered in last year's series, were the mechanisms designed to protect them.

outline.heading: Selective clarity: alcohol and cheating
outline.gist: The Prophet and companions were completely clear on outcomes; today we are clear on some prohibitions and have left others behind. Do not drink is vital, but do not cheat is equally important, if not more.

outline.heading: The cheating student cheats forever
outline.gist: Cheating that starts in school continues as a senior student, consultant, employee and spouse; a Muslim does not lie or cheat. Alcohol stays absolutely haram; the problem is what we dropped.

outline.heading: Raise the dropped standard, do not lower the kept one
outline.gist: When one value is in place and another is not, restore the neglected one rather than degrade the other. Jahiliyyah lived on convenient exemptions; the Prophet hit the brakes and they changed.

outline.heading: History's most real transformation
outline.gist: The companions' change is the most remarkable transformation of human beings ever recorded, with no superpowers involved. Study Ja'far and his peers: the outcomes were achieved, and we can do the same once we define them.

outline.heading: Interlude
Children need living examples at home
outline.gist: Parents bring children to the masjid to be made good Muslims, but theory and historical examples only work so long without a modern one. If they do not experience Islam through you, they leave after years of teaching and memorisation; it fails every time.

outline.heading: Know what we preach; metrics reveal shortcomings
outline.gist: We must practise what we preach, but first understand what we preach. This is not about beating yourself up: you cannot know a shortcoming without knowing the metric.

outline.heading: Humility that fuels improvement
outline.gist: Knowing where you fall short humbles the heart, and that humility generates strength, compassion and motivation to improve, rather than everyone offering their own suggestions.

outline.heading: Outro

e0Aw3E1GK-8.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Honesty, Episode 9
e0Aw3E1GK-8.one_line: Applying self-honesty to one's faith in Allah and to one's real values, then beginning muraqabah: observing actions, emotions and thoughts.
e0Aw3E1GK-8.summary: The sheikh says the whole series has been building toward the two places self-honesty matters most: one's relationship with Allah and one's value system. Many people enjoy believing that they believe, but a superficial acceptance, like the Bedouins told to say they had submitted because faith had not yet entered their hearts, collapses under hardship or a troubling doubt. One must diagnose honestly whether iman is fully settled, because no one fixes what they think is already fine; losing faith is the only true calamity. On values he describes three levels: what we tell people, what we tell ourselves, and the black box of what we actually believe, which explains repeated sins like looking at haram or gossip. Children and spouses see the true values behind our fronts, while the Prophet was loved more the closer people came. He assigns a daily reflection on emerging from the grave with nothing, to find which flaws truly worry us and whether they are the right ones. He then introduces muraqabah: observe one sin, log its pattern, then the emotions and thoughts feeding it. In answering questions he stresses accepting the deen's priority list, such as not worrying about sunnah prayers while taking bribes.

outline.heading: Where self-honesty matters most
outline.gist: The series has been building toward self-honesty about one's relationship with Allah and one's value system.

outline.heading: Claiming belief versus having it
outline.gist: Many enjoy believing that they believe; a crisis or near-death experience exposes how much faith is really there.

outline.heading: Islam on the tongue, iman in the heart
outline.gist: The Bedouins were told to say they had submitted since faith had not entered their hearts; ideas can float in the periphery without sinking in.

outline.heading: Why people lose their faith
outline.gist: People who leave after decades never honestly checked their iman; a troubling hadith or historical report shakes only a superficial belief.

outline.heading: Iman that seeing would not increase
outline.gist: An early imam said seeing Paradise would increase his reverence and longing but not his iman; diagnose honestly how far you are from that.

outline.heading: Struggling is natural, faking is not
outline.gist: Wrestling with belief while growing up is normal; the problem is claiming certainty for show instead of working on it.

outline.heading: This is between Me and My servant
outline.gist: When we recite 'You alone we worship', Allah's reply means the claim is still to be proven.

outline.heading: Turning on the headlights
outline.gist: Self-honesty shows where you stand with Allah; losing iman is the only real calamity, which is why we seek knowledge and good company.

outline.heading: Three levels of values
outline.gist: Values we project to others, values we tell ourselves we hold, and the values we actually hold.

outline.heading: The black box: looking at haram
outline.gist: People affirm looking at haram is forbidden yet keep doing it because their real belief is a long list of excuses.

outline.heading: The black box: gossip
outline.gist: Gossip continues because deep down we think it is minor or deserved, not that it is eating a dead brother's flesh.

outline.heading: Mistakes versus patterns
outline.gist: A repeated mistake usually means you do not really believe it is a problem or think you are exempt.

outline.heading: Children follow your real values
outline.gist: A heavy smoker who forbids his son to smoke fails because children pick up what is in the box, not what is projected.

outline.heading: Feedback from someone who dislikes you
outline.gist: The next step would have been to listen, without defending, to someone who does not like you.

outline.heading: Your spouse sees through the front
outline.gist: A spouse of many years knows your reality; the fronts men keep up are transparent to those close to them.

outline.heading: The closer you came, the more you loved him
outline.gist: Unlike celebrities who keep people at a distance, the Prophet's closest companions and Aisha gave the warmest testimony, and no one spoke against him after his death.

outline.heading: Changing a value begins with admitting it
outline.gist: To drop a bad habit you must first admit privately that you do not see it as a problem.

outline.heading: Exercise: who comes out of the grave
outline.gist: Daily, imagine being resurrected with no house, job, clothes or titles, and describe honestly who that person is.

outline.heading: Your worries become your priorities
outline.gist: The flaws that worry you in that scene become the targets to work on first.

outline.heading: Are you worried about the right things?
outline.gist: Check whether those worries are what you will actually be asked about, or a deeper delusion.

outline.heading: The same person now and then
outline.gist: The goal is no gap between who you are now and who is resurrected, since Allah speaks to you alone without name or support.

outline.heading: Muraqabah: actions, emotions, thoughts
outline.gist: From Allah's name ar-Raqib; observe actions first, then emotions, and thoughts last as they are hardest.

outline.heading: Observe one sin and log its pattern
outline.gist: Choose one sin, such as gossip, and record when, where and how often it happens.

outline.heading: Then the emotions and thoughts behind it
outline.gist: Track the frustration that precedes gossip, then the blaming thoughts that feed the feeling.

outline.heading: Don't let the ego slip it under the radar
outline.gist: The ego wants mistakes brushed off; pause, document and quantify instead of hiding flaws to look good.

outline.heading: Interlude
Admitting the black-box belief
outline.gist: Some values match revelation and must be preserved; others hide narratives like 'I'll be forgiven', and acknowledging them is half the battle.

outline.heading: Interlude
Question: observing without stopping
outline.gist: At this stage logging the frequency and circumstances matters more than succeeding in stopping.

outline.heading: Accept the deen's priority list
outline.gist: A scholar's job is ranking what matters; the ego wants a sheikh or algorithm to validate its own values.

outline.heading: Worrying about the wrong things
outline.gist: Someone anxious about sunnah prayers while taking bribes has it backwards; harming people's blood, wealth and honour ranks high.
