30:20.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنۡ خَلَقَكُم مِّن تُرَابࣲ ثُمَّ إِذَآ أَنتُم بَشَرࣱ تَنتَشِرُونَ
30:20.en: And of His signs is this: He created you of dust, and behold you human beings, ranging widely

30:21.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنۡ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا لِّتَسۡكُنُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيۡنَكُم مَّوَدَّةࣰ وَرَحۡمَةًۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
30:21.en: And of His signs is this: He created for you helpmeets from yourselves that ye might find rest in them, and He ordained between you love and mercy. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who reflect

30:22.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ خَلۡقُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱخۡتِلَٰفُ أَلۡسِنَتِكُمۡ وَأَلۡوَٰنِكُمۡۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّلۡعَٰلِمِينَ
30:22.en: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and colours. Lo! herein indeed are portents for men of knowledge

30:23.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ مَنَامُكُم بِٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ وَٱبۡتِغَآؤُكُم مِّن فَضۡلِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَسۡمَعُونَ
30:23.en: And of His signs is your slumber by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who heed

30:24.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ يُرِيكُمُ ٱلۡبَرۡقَ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعࣰ ا وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَيُحۡيِۦ بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَآۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
30:24.en: And of His signs is this: He showeth you the lightning for a fear and for a hope, and sendeth down water from the sky, and thereby quickeneth the earth after her death. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who understand

7:189.ar: ۞هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفۡسࣲ وَٰحِدَةࣲ وَجَعَلَ مِنۡهَا زَوۡجَهَا لِيَسۡكُنَ إِلَيۡهَاۖ فَلَمَّا تَغَشَّىٰهَا حَمَلَتۡ حَمۡلًا خَفِيفࣰ ا فَمَرَّتۡ بِهِۦۖ فَلَمَّآ أَثۡقَلَت دَّعَوَا ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُمَا لَئِنۡ ءَاتَيۡتَنَا صَٰلِحࣰ ا لَّنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
7:189.en: He it is Who did create you from a single soul, and therefrom did make his mate that he might take rest in her. And when he covered her she bore a light burden, and she passed (unnoticed) with it, but when it became heavy they cried unto Allah, their Lord, saying: If thou givest unto us aright we shall be of the thankful

35:27.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا بِهِۦ ثَمَرَٰتࣲ مُّخۡتَلِفًا أَلۡوَٰنُهَاۚ وَمِنَ ٱلۡجِبَالِ جُدَدُۢ بِيضࣱ وَحُمۡرࣱ مُّخۡتَلِفٌ أَلۡوَٰنُهَا وَغَرَابِيبُ سُودࣱ‏
35:27.en: Hast thou not seen that Allah causeth water to fall from the sky, and We produce therewith fruit of divers hues; and among the hills are streaks white and red, of divers hues, and (others) raven-black

49:13.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرࣲ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ شُعُوبࣰ ا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَىٰكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
49:13.en: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware

11:118.ar: وَلَوۡ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ لَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰۖ وَلَا يَزَالُونَ مُخۡتَلِفِينَ
11:118.en: And if thy Lord had willed, He verily would have made mankind one nation, yet they cease not differing

11:119.ar: إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ رَبُّكَۚ وَلِذَٰلِكَ خَلَقَهُمۡۗ وَتَمَّتۡ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ لَأَمۡلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ ٱلۡجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجۡمَعِينَ

QnD_WdPChcg.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Ar-Rum (30:20-23)
QnD_WdPChcg.one_line: Signs as laws: our earthly nature, the need for a spouse, diversity of tongues and colours, and the balance between sleep and seeking Allah's bounty.
QnD_WdPChcg.summary: He insists the Quran must be read with the meanings words carried at revelation, not today's usage. Being made from dust means our instincts stay earthly, so we must stay humble and keep refining the self that mixes divine spirit with clay. Verse 21 makes the need for a spouse a law: humans are unsettled until they find tranquility in a partner, with a unique affection and mercy. A long Harvard study found that relationships, not income above a modest level, drive happiness. Parents who forget their own youth and block lawful marriage push children toward the unlawful, and societies that denied this law now face indecency, late marriage and worse. Verse 22 ties the diversity of languages and peoples to the creation of the heavens and earth: Islam removes what is harmful in each culture but never erases identities, and erasing a people, as colonizers did to Indigenous nations here, is a crime that cannot prosper. Verse 23 places sleep and seeking bounty across both night and day to teach balance; drawing on psychiatric practice and his work with youth, he warns that young people who stay up all night and waste their days cannot produce anything, and urges a disciplined routine like the Prophet's.

outline.heading: Read Quranic words with their original meanings
outline.gist: Applying modern meanings of words to the Quran has misled some who lacked command of Arabic.

outline.heading: 'Lisan' versus 'lughah'
outline.gist: The Quran uses 'lisan' for language; 'lughah' was not a word in common use then.

outline.heading: Dust means our instincts stay earthly
outline.gist: We are spirit mixed with clay; the earthly side follows natural drives, so we must be humble and keep reforming the self.

outline.heading: A creature that must refine itself
outline.gist: Unlike jinn and angels, humans carry great capacity for good and evil and stay captive to the self unless they purify it.

outline.heading: Spouses 'from among yourselves'
outline.gist: Seeing people replace human companionship with pets showed him why the verse specifies a spouse of our own kind.

outline.heading: Sukun: settling an inner unrest
outline.gist: Each person is unsettled until finding a spouse to rest in; affection and mercy are added on top of this tranquility.

outline.heading: The Harvard study on happiness
outline.gist: A seventy-year study found income beyond a modest level adds no happiness, while the quality of relationships, above all with a spouse, does.

outline.heading: Why people stay in ruined countries
outline.gist: Most refuse to leave because their happiness lies in the people they love.

outline.heading: Divorce as mercy and peace of mind
outline.gist: Because this relationship decides one's peace, Allah permitted divorce; a home full of fighting leaves even a king miserable.

outline.heading: Wants versus needs
outline.gist: Happiness needs little: daily bread, health, covering and a spouse to rest in; the self wants everything.

outline.heading: 'Signs for people who reflect' as laws to obey
outline.gist: Reading 'ayat' at the end of the verse as laws means one should not let young people stay unmarried into their thirties.

outline.heading: Scholars who never married
outline.gist: Al-Nawawi, consumed by knowledge and writing, and Ibn Taymiyyah had particular reasons; the prophetic norm is that men and women marry.

outline.heading: A love unlike any other
outline.gist: The affection and mercy between spouses differ in kind from love of parents, siblings or friends.

outline.heading: Parents who forget their own youth
outline.gist: We are incomplete alone; parents who block the lawful path while forgetting their own need answer to Allah.

outline.heading: Deny this law and society breaks
outline.gist: Denying the need to marry spread indecency and confusion in sexuality, divorce and harassment; Muslims once married their children early and helped them.

outline.heading: Both Adam and Eve were unsettled
outline.gist: Al-A'raf shows each was in unrest until resting in the other, whichever was created first.

outline.heading: Verse 22: 'colours' means kinds and peoples
outline.gist: In Quranic Arabic colours meant types and species; tongues are our ways of expression, the gift of bayan.

outline.heading: Diversity is by design
outline.gist: Linking it to the creation of heavens and earth shows Allah intended diverse tongues and cultures; Islam is not a mould.

outline.heading: Follow the Prophet in values, not in local customs
outline.gist: Some preachers wrongly try to erase identities; we imitate his character and principles, not seventh-century Arabian culture.

outline.heading: A mosque of many nations
outline.gist: Unlike Saudi Arabia or Syria, his mosque here gathers a dozen nationalities, and Eid shows the beauty of national dress.

outline.heading: Islam keeps the good in each culture
outline.gist: A French Muslim stays French; occupiers who tried to erase languages failed or bred hatred.

outline.heading: Respecting others' faiths and languages
outline.gist: Muslim rule protected churches and local tongues, scholars wrote in Persian, and we must speak the language of the people we live among.

outline.heading: Two readings and the crime of erasing a people
outline.gist: 'For the worlds' and 'for those of knowledge'; the destruction of Indigenous peoples here defied this law and its work stays cursed.

outline.heading: Summary of the first three laws
outline.gist: Be humble as dust, honour your need for a spouse, respect the diversity of others.

outline.heading: Minorities and the strength of Arabic
outline.gist: Muslim lands mistreated Amazigh, Kurds and Turkmen; letting people keep their languages strengthens Arabic, whose expressive power far exceeds English.

outline.heading: Verses 23-24 recited: sleep and seeking bounty
outline.gist: Both sleep and seeking bounty happen by night and by day.

outline.heading: The law of balance between rest and work
outline.gist: Night leans to sleep and day to seeking, but the phrasing teaches a balance one must keep.

outline.heading: A man must go out every day
outline.gist: Sleeping life away brings misery even with inherited wealth; a man who stays home all day loses his mind and tires his wife.

outline.heading: The psychiatrist's routine
outline.gist: In psychiatric consults the advice was always the same: wake by nine, wash, dress, eat breakfast and leave the house, or no medicine helps.

outline.heading: The balance Allah set, heard and obeyed
outline.gist: The mizan must not be upset; 'people who hear' means those who hear and obey.

outline.heading: Young people who do not sleep
outline.gist: Mentoring youth with Sheikh al-Janabi revealed poor sleep as the main problem; few attend Sunday Fajr, and the Prophet slept, prayed and napped in order.

outline.heading: A law for believer and atheist alike
outline.gist: Whoever organizes sleep and work finds stability and happiness.

outline.heading: No tazkiyah without work
outline.gist: His teachers first asked what he did for a living; idle summers should be filled with work, volunteering or study.

outline.heading: Read the next verse on your own
outline.gist: Natural, human and behavioural laws reward those who respect them.
